lines.says: The theorem asserts, with no premises, the proposition that the code calls EveryCharacter. Unfolded, it says that for every nonzero natural number N, every Dirichlet character χ of level N with complex values and every complex number s with real part greater than 1/2, if χ is not the trivial character or s is not 1, then the library value DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s is not zero. A wrapper theorem in the module Main, named LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re, is folded into this line and asserts a proposition called DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf whose body the dossier does not show.
lines.conclusion: For all N ≠ 0, all χ of level N and all complex s with Re(s) > 1/2 and (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1), the value LFunction χ s is nonzero.
lines.notation: ∀ N ∈ ℕ with N ≠ 0, ∀ χ a Dirichlet character mod N with values in ℂ, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, 1/2 < Re(s) ⇒ (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) ⇒ LFunction(χ, s) ≠ 0
lines.suggests: The names suggest that LFunction is the analytically continued Dirichlet L-function, in which case the statement says no Dirichlet L-function has a zero with real part above 1/2, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis that includes the Riemann zeta function at N = 1, and the wrapper name suggests it restates the same claim.
lines.why: The statement of the head and the one definition it names are shown in full, and the names of the standard library remain unfolded. The proposition DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf of the wrapper also remains unfolded in the dossier. The dossier shows nothing about the proof or the axioms it relies on.

lines.says: The theorem says that if the proposition Row0b holds for the notion Rc that sends a pair (h, rc) to the condition IsRecT h rc, then EveryCharacter holds. The premise Row0b says that for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, every natural number a ≥ 1, every π of type CuspSub E a and every χ of type HChar over the maximal real subfield of E, if the class of π satisfies a condition that the code calls IsRegAlg and the pair (π, χ) satisfies PolarizedPair, then there exist a group homomorphism r from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_a(Qbar l), an integer wt and a function HT from the ring embeddings of E into Qbar l to multisets of integers such that PropsB Rc π ι r wt HT holds. The conclusion is the nonvanishing statement of line 1.

lines.notation: [∀ E CM number field, ∀ Ω algebraic closure of E, ∀ l prime, ∀ ι a ring isomorphism Qbar_l ≅ ℂ, ∀ a ≥ 1, ∀ π ∈ CuspSub(E, a), ∀ χ ∈ HChar(E⁺), IsRegAlg([π]) ⇒ PolarizedPair(π, χ) ⇒ ∃ r from Aut_E(Ω) to GL_a(Qbar_l), ∃ wt ∈ ℤ, ∃ HT, PropsB(IsRecT, π, ι, r, wt, HT)] ⇒ [∀ N ≠ 0, ∀ χ mod N, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, 1/2 < Re(s) ⇒ (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) ⇒ LFunction(χ, s) ≠ 0]
lines.suggests: The names suggest that the premise is the existence of l-adic Galois representations attached to regular algebraic polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_a over CM fields, with local-global compatibility measured against a local Langlands reciprocity map, and that the conclusion is the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions.

The bundle has three fields, of which the first and third are both the proposition Row and the second is RecTExists, which says that for every number field E, algebraic closure Ω, valuation subring A of Ω and prime w of the integers of E with a proof h of IsPlaceOver A w, there exists a map rc satisfying IsRecT h rc. The conclusion is that LFunction χ s ≠ 0 for every nonzero N, every complex Dirichlet character χ of level N and every complex s with real part above 1/2 such that χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1.

deeper.says: The theorem assumes nine propositions taken as hypotheses. Seven of them are statements of published results that the code names GlobalArtinReciprocity, SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, DiscreteSeriesCover, HarishChandraModules, CuspRapidDecay, CasselmanWallach and DiscreteSeriesClassification, and two are the eventual bounds SurjectiveOntoX and LambdaLowerBound₂. Under these hypotheses it considers any proof hL of the proposition RecTExists, any norm choice extension N over hL, any S of type SExt, any Γ of type GeoP and any property NN of family classes, and it lets p be the parameter record parametersOfExtension N S Γ, which is the four-part record made of RX, N, S and Γ. If p satisfies every part of the record OpenParameterStatements, and LinkedAt holds at p for the three row conditions CovolumeBoundThirdPlaceSeries, FunctionalCondition and the slot norm condition for NN, then the record AllRowsAlt holds. That record is built from the base predicate KPx, the slots IsBuiltE p.s and IsGoodE p.s, the linkage BundleLinkage p, the property NN and the side condition DefiniteSideCondition. In unfolded form, AllRowsAlt says that each of a long list of row conditions (class count bound, J-invariant, instance rank, divisor, primitivity, Lp, order, torsion-free and others) is linked at p in the same sense as LinkedAt. The list is cut in the dossier, so further fields that may use NN and DefiniteSideCondition are not visible.

The second is the rank condition RanksRow with constant 3. The third is the row condition LoopRowS with constant 3 and the selector sel. Under these assumptions the property Closed holds for 𝒞. There is a threshold ε₁ > 0 such that, for every eps with 0 < eps ≤ ε₁, there is an object K of the type the code calls TransportedAlt with this property. For every family Fm of the type FamP eps and every real number CH, if Fm satisfies the bundle of conditions FamHyp and the condition Fm.Large K CH, and Fm also satisfies the divisibility condition DIVinN, then there is a real C₀ ≥ 0 and a cutoff x₀ such that, at every admissible point p over every x > Fm.x1 with x ≥ x₀ and every index i, if p satisfies PointConditions' and the condition More, then for every C ≥ C₀ the relation ON holds between p.S false and p.N C CH. deeper.says: The theorem says that if the hypothesis bundle the code calls UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses holds, then a conclusion follows for every proof hL of the proposition RecTExists and for every real number cDep. RecTExists says that for every number field E, every algebraic closure Ω of E, every valuation subring A of Ω and every nonzero prime w of the ring of integers of E that A lies over, there is a map rc that satisfies a condition the code calls IsRecT. The hypothesis bundle is the joint assertion of a long list of named statements, most of them labelled as published results, such as Bernstein's irreducibility of products of unitary representations, Chebotarev's density theorem in a degree one form, and global Artin reciprocity. The conclusion is that the parameter record parametersOfDependence hL cDep satisfies OpenParameterStatements. This means that twelve row or slot conditions each hold in the sense the code calls LinkedAt for that record.

deeper.says: Assume fourteen propositions that the code names after published results, from HarishChandraFinite through the second proposition called SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, which lives in the HeckeCharacterZeroLocus namespace. Then for every proof hL of the statement RecTExists, every norm-choice extension N over hL, every S of type SExt and every geometric predicate Γ of type GeoP, two claims hold for the parameter record p = parametersOfExtension N S Γ, which is the four-part record made of RX, N, S and Γ. The first claim is LinkedAt p r, where r takes a slot Q and a linkage L to the proposition Row Q L (AtAll R). Here R is the test that, for a bundle b, holds when the condition MIstar2 holds for the complex datum b.B.Q.Rl.toCx3 b.B.Q.F, with arguments b.B.Q.F.eV applied to that datum's zs and b.B.Q.sEE. The second claim is LinkedAt p RowMultiplicityCondition, which is the same row statement with the test wrapped by an operator the code calls Ind.EvW in place of AtAll. Unfolded, each claim says that there is a slot R0 such that a condition the code calls LargeBaseCondition holds for KPx, IsBuiltE p.s and R0, and such that the row statement holds at the slot that is the pointwise conjunction of IsGoodE p.s with R0, paired with the linkage BundleLinkage p.
premises: the proposition HarishChandraFinite, which says that the complex span of the set that the code calls forms θ V U ε fr ρ c is finite-dimensional, for every D7 record, every family θ with IsInfFam θ, every open subgroup U, every frame family and every family of continuous finite-dimensional representations
the proposition CuspRapidDecay, which says that cuspidal automorphic functions with the listed smoothness and moderate growth satisfy a condition the code calls IsRapidDecay
the proposition DiscreteSeriesCover, which says that for p + q ≥ 1 every representation of type DSRep T is unitarily equivalent to one in a family indexed by parameters
the proposition HarishChandraModules, which is HarishChandraModulesOn T for all p, q with p + q ≥ 1 and all T, together with KFiniteAnalyticUJ
the proposition CasselmanWallach, which says that a (g,K)-map from an irreducible unitary representation extends to a unique smooth map with closed image and Sobolev-type bounds
the proposition HoweUnram, which is a statement about unramified local pairs and spans of vectors fixed by integral matrices
the proposition WeilRepresentationUnitaryPair, which says that a Weil datum ω exists for the given characters and Hermitian spaces
the proposition WeilSiegelFormulaUnitary, which states theta-integral convergence and, when 2·rank A < rank B, an identity between an Eisenstein coset sum and a theta average

the proposition GlobalTheory.Published.SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, which gives theta-integral integrability and the condition that the code calls Eis.EisValueAt whenever rank A < rank B and rank B ≤ 2·rank A and rank A + wittIdx B < rank B
the proposition DoublingMethodLocalZetaIntegrals, which is by definition the proposition the code calls ResidueKilled.DM
the proposition UnramifiedDoublingGL, which says that the unramified doubling zeta integral on GL(n) equals a product of two L-factors at s + 1/2 times a normalising factor once Re s exceeds some s₀
the proposition DiscreteSeriesClassification, which classifies square-integrable irreducible unitary representations by Harish-Chandra parameters
the proposition StrongApproxSU, which is strong approximation for special unitary groups of nondegenerate Hermitian matrices of size at least 2 over CM extensions

the proposition HeckeCharacterZeroLocus.SiegelWeilU.SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, which says that a condition the code calls SiegelWeilAt holds for every CM extension and every nondegenerate Hermitian matrix
deeper.conclusion: For all hL, N, S and Γ, the parameter record parametersOfExtension N S Γ is linked both to the row statement that every selected bundle satisfies MIstar2 at every index beyond the threshold and to RowMultiplicityCondition.

deeper.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names hint at the following reading. The premises would be published theorems of automorphic representation theory, such as Harish-Chandra finiteness, Casselman–Wallach, the Siegel–Weil formula and strong approximation, taken as hypotheses. The conclusion would then say that the bundles produced by the theta-lift construction satisfy an isometric-period unit condition MIstar2 at every index, and eventually in the sense of EvW, so that the row multiplicity condition holds.

deeper.says: The theorem says that if fourteen given statements all hold, then a certain conclusion holds for every proof hL of the statement the code calls RecTExists and for every parameter record p built over hL. The first thirteen are statements from the Published and Hk3 namespaces, such as a Harish-Chandra finiteness statement, a Casselman–Wallach statement, a Siegel–Weil statement and a strong approximation statement for special unitary groups. The fourteenth is RowDiag applied to a predicate E. Here E D L C' holds when D has size data whose scale has L as its field L and whose constant CGam satisfies 1 ≤ CGam and 8·CGam ≤ C', and when for every word u the complex dimension of the space D.s.Cu u equals duStar·(T^k − 1)^f. For each such hL and p there is one more premise, namely that for every context K and every point q of type WPt p.s K the record type RXs q.x.what₂ has an element. The conclusion is RowE for the slot IsGoodE p.s and the linkage BundleLinkage p, with a target predicate that requires MIstar2 to hold for the data read off each linked bundle b.
premises: HarishChandraFinite holds. For every D in D7, every family θ with IsInfFam θ, every V in HSp D, every open subgroup U of GA D V, all families ε and fr with IsFrameFam V ε fr, every family of finite-dimensional representations ρ with IsContRep for each of them and every c, the complex span of the set the code calls forms θ V U ε fr ρ c is finite-dimensional

CuspRapidDecay holds. For every D in D7, every family θ with IsInfFam θ, every V in HSp D and every family e with IsExpFam θ V e, every function φ from GA D V to the complex numbers that satisfies IsAutFun V φ, IsSmoothInf V e φ, IsUnifModerate θ V e φ and IsCuspFun V φ satisfies the condition the code calls IsRapidDecay θ V φ

DiscreteSeriesCover holds. For all p and q with 1 ≤ p + q and every T in GrpData p q there is a family D indexed by the parameters lam with IsParam lam, such that each D lam has the types lam and every R in DSRep T is unitarily equivalent to some D lam
HarishChandraModules holds. HarishChandraModulesOn T holds for all p and q with 1 ≤ p + q and every T, and KFiniteAnalyticUJ holds

CasselmanWallach holds. Every (g,K)-map T₀ from an irreducible unitary representation to a smooth moderate representation extends to a unique smooth G-map T on smooth vectors, the image of the smooth vectors under T is closed, and Sobolev-type norms are bounded by a continuous seminorm when T₀ is nonzero on some K-finite vector

HoweUnram holds. For every local pair as in LocPair and every nonzero vector s with LocVac ρ s whose translates ρ x s span M, every vector fixed by the integral points of the first unitary group lies in the span of the translates of s under the second group, and symmetrically for the second group
WeilRepresentationUnitaryPair holds. For suitable characters ψ, χS and χT there exists ω with IsWeilDatumO ψ S T χS χT ω

WeilSiegelFormulaUnitary holds. This is a statement about the absolute convergence of theta integrals and the equality of a Siegel Eisenstein coset sum with the average of the theta integral when 2·rank A < rank B
SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent holds. This is a statement giving integrability of the theta lift and the condition EisValueAt in the range rank A < rank B ≤ 2·rank A with rank A + wittIdx B < rank B
a condition that the code calls DoublingMethodLocalZetaIntegrals holds, defined as ResidueKilled.DM

UnramifiedDoublingGL holds. For a nonarchimedean local field k of characteristic 0, a Haar measure giving the integral points measure 1, and a representation with Satake parameter α and zonal function ω, there is s₀ such that for Re s > s₀ the doubling integral converges and equals L(s+1/2, α)·L(s+1/2, α⁻¹)·invNormFactor

DiscreteSeriesClassification holds. For each n there is a family of square-integrable irreducible unitary representations indexed by signs ε and strictly decreasing parameters lam with prescribed infinitesimal character and minimal K-type, and every square-integrable irreducible unitary representation is isometrically equivalent to one of them after a permutation

StrongApproxSU holds. For a CM extension E over F, a nondegenerate hermitian J of size at least 2 and a set of places whose support group is not compact, every adelic element of SU lies in the closure of the products of rational elements and support elements
RowDiag holds for the predicate E D L C' given by IsScaleWithBoundedGamma D L C' together with RankMu D u for every word u
for every context K and every q in WPt p.s K the type RXs q.x.what₂ is nonempty

Then VWin holds, which says that for every primitive complex Dirichlet character ψ the window statement VWinAt ψ 401 holds, in the same form as in lines 30 and 31. The bundle consists of an earlier bundle Hypotheses' with ten parts, plus five further statements named descU, cyc, cyc2, quat and ssR.

lines.says: With no premises, the statement Row0b holds for the notion recT, which is the notion IsRecT. In words, for every CM number field E with an algebraic closure Ω, every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from an algebraic closure of the l-adic numbers to ℂ, every a ≥ 1, every π of type CuspSub E a and every χ of type HChar on the maximal real subfield of E, if the class of π satisfies IsRegAlg and the pair satisfies PolarizedPair π χ, then there exist a group homomorphism r from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_a over the l-adic algebraic closure, an integer wt, and a function HT assigning a multiset of integers to each field embedding of E into the l-adic algebraic closure, such that PropsB recT π ι r wt HT holds. PropsB asserts that r is continuous, that r satisfies IsSSRep, a condition AwayB at each finite prime not containing l, two explicit identities for HT, and a condition AboveB.
lines.conclusion: Row0b recT holds, that is, every π over a CM field with IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair has some r, wt and HT with PropsB recT π ι r wt HT
lines.notation: ∀ E CM number field, ∀ Ω algebraic closure of E, ∀ l prime, ∀ ι ∈ (Qbar_l ≅ ℂ as rings), ∀ a ≥ 1, ∀ π ∈ CuspSub(E, a), ∀ χ ∈ HChar(E⁺), IsRegAlg([π]) ∧ PolarizedPair(π, χ) ⇒ ∃ r ∈ Hom(Aut_E(Ω), GL_a(Qbar_l)), ∃ wt ∈ ℤ, ∃ HT ∈ ((E → Qbar_l) → Multisets(ℤ)), PropsB(recT, π, ι, r, wt, HT). Inside PropsB, r is continuous ∧ IsSSRep(r) ∧ (∀ w ∌ l, ∀ A, ∀ h ∈ IsPlaceOver(A, w), ∀ rc, IsRecT(h, rc) ⇒ ∀ σ, IsLocComp(π, w, σ) ⇒ AwayB(wdOf(h, ι, r), rc(algNorm σ))) ∧ (∀ τ, HT(τ) = {(a − 1)/2 − z, z ∈ infChar([π], ι∘τ)} as multisets in ℂ) ∧ (∀ τ, HT(τ∘c) = {wt − n, n ∈ HT(τ)}, c complex conjugation of E) ∧ (∀ P, AI, LocTied(l, P, AI) nonempty ⇒ ∀ w, A, h, O, Bw, hj, AboveB(recT, π, ι, r, HT, P, h, Bw, hj))
unopened: IsPlaceOver, WD, IrrGL, wdOf, algNorm, LocPrime, LocAinf, LocTied, LocBridge, Induces
lines.suggests: The names suggest the existence of l-adic Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_a over a CM field, semisimple and continuous, compatible with a local Langlands correspondence at primes away from l, with Hodge–Tate weights determined by the infinitesimal character, and with a p-adic Hodge theoretic condition at primes above l.
lines.why: The quantifier structure, the existence claim and the two weight identities are fully visible, but IsRegAlg, IsSSRep, AwayB, AboveB, LawsT and the underlying automorphic types are shown without bodies.

lines.says: Assume the statement that the code calls TLiftK. Then Row0b recT holds, which is exactly the conclusion of line 33. That is, for every CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, prime l, ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, a ≥ 1, π of type CuspSub E a and χ of type HChar on the maximal real subfield, if IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair π χ hold then some homomorphism r, integer wt and function HT satisfy PropsB recT π ι r wt HT.

lines.conclusion: Row0b recT holds, that is, every π over a CM field with IsRegAlg and PolarizedPair has some r, wt and HT with PropsB recT π ι r wt HT
lines.notation: TLiftK ⇒ Row0b(recT), where TLiftK ⇔ ∀ E CM, ∀ B ∈ Base(E⁺, E), GoodK(cj, B) ⇒ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ X ∈ Spc(n), X.J = 1 ⇒ IsHerm(X, cj, B, n, 0) ⇒ ∃ d₀ ∈ ℕ, ∀ d ≥ d₀, ∀ W ∈ Spc(d), ∀ δ ∈ E, W.J = δ·I_d ⇒ IsSkew(W, cj, B, d, 0) ⇒ ∀ χX, χW, mX, mW, IsHecke(χX) ⇒ IsHecke(χW) ⇒ ResEtaPow(K, χX, n) ⇒ ResEtaPow(K, χW, d) ⇒ HasExp(B.emb, χX, mX) ⇒ HasExp(B.emb, χW, mW) ⇒ ∀ U, ∀ lam, IsAutRepU(U) ⇒ (∀ w, HasWeightAt(U, B.emb(w), lam(w))) ⇒ (∀ w, k, d + mW(w) ≤ 2·lam(w)_k) ⇒ ∃ U', IsLift(B, χX, χW, mX, mW, lam, U, U'), with K the image of (E⁺)ˣ in the unit group of the adele ring of E⁺, and Row0b(recT) ⇔ ∀ E CM, Ω, l, ι, a ≥ 1, π, χ, IsRegAlg([π]) ∧ PolarizedPair(π, χ) ⇒ ∃ r, wt, HT, PropsB(recT, π, ι, r, wt, HT)
lines.suggests: The names suggest that a theta lifting statement between unitary groups of sizes n and d, for all sufficiently large d, is enough to construct the Galois representations of line 33.
lines.why: Both the premise and the conclusion have fully visible quantifier structure, but the key conditions IsHerm, IsSkew, IsLiftWt, LocPair, HasWeightAt, IsRegAlg, AwayB and AboveB are opaque.

lines.says: With no premises, the statement GeoOne holds. GeoOne takes a CM number field E with algebraic closure Ω, a prime l, a ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, an odd a, a natural number d with FieldOK E l d, an x in E with x² = −d, a finite set T of primes of E none of which satisfies IsSplitAt, two primes w₀ and v' of E that contain l, lie over different primes of the maximal real subfield and satisfy OneK x w₀ v', a finite set S of primes, and a space U of complex functions on UA E a satisfying AutOffT T U, TyEll E l a w₀ U, SphOffU w₀ S U, SatU U v' B for some B, and LacWtAt ι v' U. It concludes three things, namely that some size dd and homomorphism ρ from the automorphism group of Ω over E to GL_dd(Qbar l) satisfy VBase ι d U ρ, that at every prime w with UsPl d w, not containing l and with some SatU datum there is such a ρ that also satisfies ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) for every B with SatU U w B, and that at every prime w containing l with OneK x w v', apart from w₀ and from v' and with some SatU datum, there is such a ρ with CrysAt ρ w and JumpsOcc U ι ρ w and there is such a ρ with PhiKilled ι ρ w a B for every B with SatU U w B.
lines.conclusion: GeoOne holds, a universally quantified statement whose own hypotheses and three-part conclusion are described in the entry of line 35, with each part asserting the existence of its own dd and ρ
lines.notation: ∀ E CM number field, ∀ Ω algebraic closure of E, ∀ l prime, ∀ ι ∈ (Qbar_l ≅ ℂ), ∀ a ∈ ℕ, Odd(a) ⇒ ∀ d ∈ ℕ, FieldOK(E, l, d) ⇒ ∀ x ∈ E, x² = −d ⇒ ∀ T finite set of primes of E, NonSplitSet(T) ⇒ ∀ w₀, v' primes of E, l ∈ w₀ ⇒ l ∈ v' ⇒ Apart(v', w₀) ⇒ OneK(x, w₀, v') ⇒ ∀ S finite set of primes, ∀ U ⊆ (UA(E, a) → ℂ), AutOffT(T, U) ⇒ TyEll(E, l, a, w₀, U) ⇒ SphOffU(w₀, S, U) ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, v', B)) ⇒ LacWtAt(ι, v', U) ⇒ [ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ)) ∧ (∀ w, UsPl(d, w) ⇒ l ∉ w ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ ∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ ESAt(ι, ρ, w, algSat(a, normV(w), B))) ∧ (∀ w, l ∈ w ⇒ OneK(x, w, v') ⇒ Apart(w, w₀) ⇒ Apart(w, v') ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ CrysAt(ρ, w) ∧ JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, w)) ∧ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ PhiKilled(ι, ρ, w, a, B))) ]
lines.suggests: The names suggest a geometric construction of l-adic Galois representations attached to automorphic representations of a definite unitary group of odd rank over a CM field containing an imaginary quadratic field, with the Eichler–Shimura relation at good split primes, and crystallinity, Hodge–Tate jumps and control of the crystalline Frobenius at primes above l.
lines.why: The full quantifier structure and many middle-level definitions are visible, but the innermost conditions (IsSplitAt, ImQ, SqAt, HasSatGL, IsCompAlong, IsSSRep, HTRichEx, IsCrysAt, IsJumpsAt, IsFrob, Lacunary) are shown without bodies, and nineteen further definitions were left out of the dossier.

lines.says: Assume the statement that the code calls HolomorphicLefschetzFormula, a fixed-point trace formula for pairs of finite étale maps between complex schemes. Then the statement GeoOne holds. GeoOne says that, for a CM number field E, a prime l, an odd number a and a complex space U of functions on a group UA E a meeting a list of conditions, there exist matrix representations ρ of the automorphism group of an algebraic closure of E over the field Qbar l that satisfy a condition called VBase, together with further conditions ESAt at certain primes not containing l and CrysAt, JumpsOcc and PhiKilled at certain primes containing l.
premises: HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds, which reads as follows. For every scheme Z smooth of relative dimension d over Spec ℂ and satisfying IsProjOver, every scheme Y over Spec ℂ with two maps c1 and c2 from Y to Z over Spec ℂ that are both finite and étale, every finite set F of complex points of Y that consists exactly of the points y with y followed by c1 equal to y followed by c2, and every assignment A of d by d complex matrices such that each y in F satisfies IsTan with A y and det(1 − A y) ≠ 0, and for every natural number a, all the spaces hodgeH s a b are finite dimensional over ℂ and the sum over b from 0 to d of (−1)^b times the trace of hodgeTrace for c1 composed with hodgePull for c2 on hodgeH s a b equals the sum over y in F of the coefficient of X^a in det(1 + X·A y) divided by det(1 − A y)
lines.conclusion: GeoOne holds, which reads as follows. For all E, Ω, l, ι, odd a, d with FieldOK E l d, x in E with x² = −d, T with NonSplitSet T, primes w₀ and v' containing l with Apart v' w₀ and OneK x w₀ v', every finite set S of primes and every U with AutOffT T U, TyEll at w₀, SphOffU w₀ S U, some B with SatU U v' B, and LacWtAt ι v' U, three things hold. First, some dimension dd and some ρ satisfy VBase ι d U ρ. Second, for every prime w with UsPl d w, not containing l and having some B with SatU U w B, some dd and ρ satisfy VBase and ESAt ι ρ w (algSat a (normV w) B) for every B with SatU U w B. Third, for every prime w containing l with OneK x w v', Apart w w₀, Apart w v' and some B with SatU U w B, some dd and ρ satisfy VBase, CrysAt ρ w and JumpsOcc U ι ρ w, and some possibly different dd and ρ satisfy VBase and PhiKilled ι ρ w a B for every B with SatU U w B
lines.notation: HLF ⇒ GeoOne, where HLF is [∀ Z, s ∈ Hom(Z, Spec ℂ), d ∈ ℕ, s smooth of relative dimension d, IsProjOver(s) ⇒ ∀ Y, s' ∈ Hom(Y, Spec ℂ), c1, c2 ∈ Hom(Y, Z) with c1≫s = s', c2≫s = s', c1 and c2 finite étale ⇒ ∀ finite F ⊆ CxPts(s') with (∀ y, y ∈ F ⇔ y≫c1 = y≫c2), ∀ A from CxPts(s') to M_d(ℂ) with (∀ y ∈ F, IsTan(d, c1, c2, y, A y) ∧ det(1 − A y) ≠ 0), ∀ a ∈ ℕ, (∀ b, dim_ℂ hodgeH(s, a, b) < ∞) ∧ Σ_{b=0}^{d} (−1)^b tr(hodgeTrace_{c1}(a, b) ∘ hodgePull_{c2}(a, b)) = Σ_{y ∈ F} coeff_{X^a} det(1 + X·A y) / det(1 − A y)] and GeoOne is [∀ E CM number field, Ω algebraic closure of E, l prime, ι a ring isomorphism Qbar_l ≅ ℂ, a ∈ ℕ odd, d ∈ ℕ with FieldOK(E, l, d), x ∈ E with x² = −d, T finite set of primes of O_E with NonSplitSet(T), primes w₀, v' with l ∈ w₀, l ∈ v', Apart(v', w₀), OneK(x, w₀, v'), S finite set of primes, U a ℂ-subspace of the functions UA(E, a) → ℂ with AutOffT(T, U), TyEll(E, l, a, w₀, U), SphOffU(w₀, S, U), (∃ B, SatU(U, v', B)), LacWtAt(ι, v', U) ⇒ (∃ dd, ρ ∈ Hom(Aut_E(Ω), GL_dd(Qbar_l)), VBase(ι, d, U, ρ)) ∧ (∀ w, UsPl(d, w) ⇒ l ∉ w ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ ∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ ESAt(ι, ρ, w, algSat(a, normV(w), B))) ∧ (∀ w, l ∈ w ⇒ OneK(x, w, v') ⇒ Apart(w, w₀) ⇒ Apart(w, v') ⇒ (∃ B, SatU(U, w, B)) ⇒ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ CrysAt(ρ, w) ∧ JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, w)) ∧ (∃ dd, ρ, VBase(ι, d, U, ρ) ∧ ∀ B, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ PhiKilled(ι, ρ, w, a, B)))]
lines.suggests: The names suggest that the hypothesis is the holomorphic Lefschetz fixed-point formula for a correspondence on a smooth projective complex variety acting on Hodge cohomology, and that the conclusion is the construction, in the cohomology of unitary Shimura varieties, of l-adic Galois representations attached to automorphic representations of a unitary group, with local-global compatibility at unramified split places, crystallinity, Hodge–Tate weights and a Frobenius eigenvalue relation at places above l.
lines.why: The full logical shape of both the hypothesis and GeoOne is shown, but most leaf conditions rest on names without bodies and 61 definitions were left out of the dossier.

lines.says: The theorem states, with no hypothesis, that a bundle of seventeen propositions that the code calls Steps holds. Most of the seventeen are universally quantified implications about homomorphisms ρ from the group G E Ω, for a number field E with an algebraic closure Ω, into invertible matrices over the field Qbar l, about objects H of a type HTower E with a function θ on H.Γ, or about general matrix representations of a group. One of them, CharEx, instead asserts the existence of a map L that sends pairs (χ, n) to homomorphisms from G E Ω to the units of Qbar l, and another, SatCard, concerns a function space U and a multiset B and no representation. Nearly all the conditions that these implications relate are names whose bodies this dossier does not show.
lines.conclusion: all seventeen fields of Steps hold, namely RepEx, ESStep, CrysStep, JumpStep, PhiStep, CutStep, TwES, TwCrys, TwJ, TwPhi, PhiOf, SatCard, JumpsOf, RichOf, CharEx, SSLeft and ContLeft
lines.notation: Steps = RepEx ∧ ESStep ∧ CrysStep ∧ JumpStep ∧ PhiStep ∧ CutStep ∧ TwES ∧ TwCrys ∧ TwJ ∧ TwPhi ∧ PhiOf ∧ SatCard ∧ JumpsOf ∧ RichOf ∧ CharEx ∧ SSLeft ∧ ContLeft. Throughout, E is a number field, Ω an algebraic closure of E, l a prime, ι a ring isomorphism Qbar_l ≅ ℂ, H ∈ HTower(E), θ a function H.Γ → Qbar_l, ρ ∈ Hom(G(E, Ω), GL_dd(Qbar_l)), w a prime of O_E. RepEx is [Nice(H) ⇒ ∃ dd, ρ, ρ continuous ∧ IsSSRep(ρ) ∧ IsPiece(H, θ, ρ)]. ESStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∉ w, CongAt(H, θ, w, n, ϑ), HasRoots(ι, w, n, ϑ, R) ⇒ ESAt(ι, ρ, w, R)]. CrysStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∈ w, C ∈ Cover(H, θ, Ow(w)), C.Onto ⇒ CrysAt(ρ, w)]. JumpStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∈ w, GoodAt(H, θ, w) ⇒ JOcc(ι, ρ, w, HodgeAt(ι, H, θ))]. PhiStep is [Nice(H), ρ continuous, IsPiece(H, θ, ρ), l ∈ w, CongAt(H, θ, w, n, ϑ), HasRoots(ι, w, n, ϑ, R) ⇒ PhiK(ι, ρ, w, R)]. CutStep is [for any field L and θ with values in L, Nice(H) ⇒ ∀ w, (GoodAtW(H, θ, w) ⇒ GoodAt(H, θ, w)) ∧ ∀ n, ϑ, CongAtW(H, θ, w, n, ϑ) ⇒ CongAt(H, θ, w, n, ϑ)]. With χ ∈ Hom(G(E, Ω), Qbar_l^×), ρ and χ continuous, c ∈ ℂ, m a function from embeddings E → ℂ to ℤ, and Cl(ι, rk1 χ, w, {c}, τ ↦ {m(ι∘τ)}) assumed, TwES is [l ∉ w, ESAt(ι, ρ, w, R) ⇒ ESAt(ι, tw(ρ, χ), w, R·c)], TwCrys is [CrysAt(ρ, w) ⇒ CrysAt(tw(ρ, χ), w)], TwJ is [∀ Q, JOcc(ι, ρ, w, Q) ⇒ JOcc(ι, tw(ρ, χ), w, (τ, j) ↦ Q(τ, j − m τ))], TwPhi is [PhiK(ι, ρ, w, R) ⇒ PhiK(ι, tw(ρ, χ), w, R·c)]. PhiOf is [|B| = a, PhiK(ι, ρ, w, algSat(a, normV(w), B)) ⇒ PhiKilled(ι, ρ, w, a, B)]. SatCard is [E CM, SatU(U, w, B) ⇒ |B| = a]. JumpsOf is [E CM, (∀ τ, OverPl(ι, τ, w) ⇒ ∀ lam, HasWeightAt(U, τ, lam) ⇒ ∀ j ∈ wtJumps(lam), Q(τ, j)), JOcc(ι, ρ, w, Q) ⇒ JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, w)]. RichOf is [E CM, l ∈ v, LacWtAt(ι, v, U), JumpsOcc(U, ι, ρ, v) ⇒ HTRichEx(ρ, a)]. CharEx is [∀ E, Ω, l, ι, ∃ L sending (χ ∈ HChar(E), n) to a homomorphism G(E, Ω) → Qbar_l^×, (∀ χ, n, IsAlgPos(χ, n) ⇒ L(χ, n) continuous ∧ ∀ w, χ.UnrAt(w) ⇒ Cl(ι, rk1(L(χ, n)), w, {χ.val(w)}, τ ↦ {−n(ι∘τ)})) ∧ (∀ χ, n, χ', n', IsAlgPos(χ, n) ⇒ IsAlgPos(χ', n') ⇒ L(χ, n) = L(χ', n') ⇒ χ = χ')]. SSLeft is [∀ group Γ, field k, a, b, (∀ r, s, IsSSRep(sumRep(r, s)) ⇒ IsSSRep(r)) ∧ (∀ r, r', RepIso(r, r') ⇒ IsSSRep(r) ⇒ IsSSRep(r')) ∧ (∀ r, c, IsSSRep(r) ⇒ IsSSRep(tw(r, c)))]. ContLeft is [∀ topological group Γ, field k with a topological ring structure, a, b, (∀ r, s, sumRep(r, s) continuous ⇒ r continuous) ∧ (∀ r, r', RepIso(r, r') ⇒ r continuous ⇒ r' continuous) ∧ (∀ r, c, r continuous ⇒ c continuous ⇒ tw(r, c) continuous) ∧ (∀ c, c continuous ⇒ rk1(c) continuous)]

lines.suggests: The names suggest a checklist of the steps of a construction of Galois representations from the cohomology of a tower of varieties with Hecke eigenvalues θ, covering existence of a semisimple piece, the Eichler–Shimura congruence relation away from l, crystallinity, Hodge–Tate jumps and a Frobenius relation at l, compatibility of each property with twisting by a character, Galois characters attached to algebraic Hecke characters, and the stability of semisimplicity and continuity under direct summands, isomorphism and twists. The name G E Ω suggests the automorphism group of Ω over E, which is the absolute Galois group of E.
lines.why: The conjunction and the quantifier shape of every field are visible, but almost every condition named inside the fields is shown without a body, so the mathematical content cannot be read off.

lines.says: Assume the statement that the code calls HolomorphicLefschetzFormula, a fixed-point trace formula for pairs of finite étale maps between complex schemes. Then a bundle of six propositions that the code calls KSAll holds. The six say that a base object gb with IsStd exists when D.a = 1, that the type KS L gb k is never empty when Sc D G holds, and that the tower T.tower N g obtained from any member T of KS satisfies the conditions Nice, GoodAtW and CongAtW under stated hypotheses, and that the object bcAlong (T.tower N g) τ, for a ring map τ from R to ℂ, satisfies HOcc under stated hypotheses.
premises: HolomorphicLefschetzFormula holds, which reads as follows. For every scheme Z smooth of relative dimension d over Spec ℂ and satisfying IsProjOver, every scheme Y over Spec ℂ with two maps c1 and c2 from Y to Z over Spec ℂ that are both finite and étale, every finite set F of complex points of Y that consists exactly of the points y with y followed by c1 equal to y followed by c2, and every assignment A of d by d complex matrices such that each y in F satisfies IsTan with A y and det(1 − A y) ≠ 0, and for every natural number a, all the spaces hodgeH s a b are finite dimensional over ℂ and the sum over b from 0 to d of (−1)^b times the trace of hodgeTrace for c1 composed with hodgePull for c2 on hodgeH s a b equals the sum over y in F of the coefficient of X^a in det(1 + X·A y) divided by det(1 − A y)
lines.conclusion: all six fields of KSAll hold, namely StdEx, KSEx, KSNice, KSGood, KSCong and KSHodge
lines.notation: HLF ⇒ StdEx ∧ KSEx ∧ KSNice ∧ KSGood ∧ KSCong ∧ KSHodge, with HLF as in line 36. Throughout, p is a prime, D ∈ Datum(p), G ∈ HTGroup(p), L ∈ Link(D, G). StdEx is [∀ p, D with D.a = 1, ∀ number field E, ring isomorphism e from D.F to E, ∃ gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, E), IsStd(e, gb)]. KSEx is [∀ p, D, G, L, Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ field R that is a ℚ-algebra, gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, R), k ∈ ℕ, KS(L, gb, k) ≠ ∅]. KSNice is [Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ R, gb, k, T ∈ KS(L, gb, k), N ∈ Lv(p), index type J, g from J to Mem(L, N), Nice(T.tower(N, g))]. KSGood is [Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ number field E, e from D.F to E, gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, E), IsStd(e, gb) ⇒ ∀ k, T ∈ KS(L, gb, k), N, J, field A, g from J to Mem(L, N), θ from J to A, prime w of O_E, ideal 𝔴 of O_{D.F}, IsPl(e, w, 𝔴) ⇒ GoodGrp(g, θ, 𝔴) ⇒ GoodAtW(T.tower(N, g), θ, w)]. KSCong is [same data and IsPl(e, w, 𝔴) ⇒ ∀ ϑ from ℕ to A, CongGrp(g, θ, 𝔴, ϑ) ⇒ CongAtW(T.tower(N, g), θ, w, D.n, ϑ)]. KSHodge is [Sc(D, G) ⇒ ∀ lam assigning to each embedding τ of D.F in ℂ a non-increasing function Fin(G.n) → ℕ, ∃ k ∈ ℕ, ∀ field R over ℚ, gb ∈ GBase(D.toG, R), T ∈ KS(L, gb, k), N, J, g from J to Mem(L, N), θ from J to ℂ, f from G.GAf to ℂ, IsFnL(L, N.1, f) ⇒ Spec(L, lam, L.KN(N.1), j ↦ (g j).fn, θ, f) ⇒ ∀ ring map τ from R to ℂ with τ(gb.ρ) = D.ρc and (∀ i, c, τ(gb.t_i(c)) = D.tau_i(c)), ∀ ring automorphism σ of ℂ, i₀ ∈ Fin(D.a), h from Fin(G.n) to ℕ, IsHExp(D.tau_{i₀}, epsOf(D), conjWt(σ, lam), h) ⇒ ∀ i, HOcc(bcAlong(T.tower(N, g), τ), j ↦ σ(θ j), h i)]
unopened: Sc, IsStd, IsPl, KS, Lv, Mem, GoodGrp, CongGrp
IsProjOver, CxPts, IsTan, hodgeH, hodgePull, hodgeTrace
lines.suggests: The names suggest that KS stands for a Kodaira–Spencer type package attaching to PEL data of unitary type with one distinguished embedding a tower of varieties with automorphic sheaves of weight k, and that the six fields say this package exists, is well behaved, has good reduction and a congruence relation at suitable primes, and has the Hodge numbers predicted by the weight lam, the last being where the Lefschetz formula is used. The name bcAlong suggests the base change of a tower along the ring map τ, so that the last field concerns the tower after base change to ℂ.
lines.why: The hypothesis and the quantifier shape of all six fields are shown in full, but the central objects KS, Sc, IsStd, Nice, GoodAtW, CongAtW and HOcc are shown without bodies and 24 definitions were left out.

glossary.name: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.RecTExists
glossary.what: a proposition without arguments, which is a statement and not a proved theorem
glossary.says: It is the statement that, for every number field E, every algebraic closure Ω of E, every valuation subring A of Ω, every height one prime w of the ring of integers of E, and every proof h that A lies over w, there exists a map rc for which the condition IsRecT h rc holds. The map rc goes from the type the code calls IrrGL, taken over the completion of E at w, to the type the code calls WD h. IsRecT h rc says that there exist a group homomorphism a from the object called Weil h to the units of that completion, and a proof ha that a satisfies IsLocalArtin, such that the twelve laws bundled in LawsT hold for a, ha and rc. The definition only names this statement and does not prove it.

parts.name: E Ω
parts.gloss: E is any type carrying a field structure that is a number field. Ω is any field that is an algebra over E and an algebraic closure of E.

parts.name: A
parts.gloss: A is any valuation subring of Ω, that is, a subring that contains x or the inverse of x for every nonzero x in Ω.

parts.name: w
parts.gloss: w is any element of the height one spectrum of 𝓞 E, the ring of integers of E, which is the set of its nonzero prime ideals.

parts.name: h
parts.gloss: h is a proof of IsPlaceOver A w. The dossier shows this to mean that, for every x in the ring of integers of E, the valuation attached to A of the image of x in Ω is less than 1 exactly when x lies in the prime ideal w.

parts.name: ∃ rc
parts.gloss: The statement asserts the existence of a function rc from IrrGL over the completion of E at w to WD h. IrrGL is the type of pairs of a natural number n and an element of IrrCl of the group GL of n by n matrices over that completion, where IrrCl is a quotient of the record type IrrRep (a complex vector space with a representation marked smooth and irreducible). WD h is the quotient of pairs (n, an object of type WDRep h on ℂ^n) by the relation the code calls Iso.

parts.name: IsRecT h rc
parts.gloss: This says that there exist a homomorphism a from Weil h to the units of the completion and a proof ha of IsLocalArtin h a such that LawsT a ha rc holds. IsLocalArtin has five fields named surj, cont, ord_eq, factor and glob, the first being that a is surjective. LawsT is a conjunction of twelve conditions on rc named dim, one, langlands, cusp, nu, absCentral, twist, central, dual, inj, depth and type. For example, dim says that the quantity lpDim of rc x equals the number n of x for every x, and inj says that rc x = rc y forces x = y whenever y satisfies the condition called Good.

glossary.suggests: The names suggest that this is the existence half of the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over the completion of a number field at a finite place, with rc a reciprocity map from irreducible smooth representations to Weil–Deligne representation classes, normalised by a local Artin map a. The letter T may mark a variant of the list of laws, which the text does not explain.
glossary.why: The quantifier structure, IsPlaceOver, IsRecT, and the field lists of LawsT and IsLocalArtin are fully visible, but many names inside those laws (such as Weil, WDRep, Good and TypeLaw) were not opened in the dossier, which reached its limit of 60,000 characters partway through level 3.

glossary.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.D7
glossary.what: a record type (a Lean structure) with 141 fields, mixing data and conditions on that data
glossary.says: D7 is a record type with no parameters, and an object of it is one large bundle of data together with proofs of conditions tying the data together. It starts from a rank record R, a host record over R, a family of Hermitian spaces sp, a rows record what₂, and a family of members mem u indexed by the words of what₂ with a base word u₀. It then asks that the field what₂.LL is a totally complex number field, Galois over ℚ, with a star operation, and it adds lattice data div, a commutative group Dt with characters muTil and chiD, a record s, local theories loc, locA and locT at every prime, a chain of records nd, ntw, naut, nbc, nexp, ntypes and nth, form data fm, a measure record cd, jet data jet and extra data gx and gat. The conditions are mostly equalities and equivalences that identify pieces of one record with pieces of another, for example the two formulas that give rhoDet as the inverse of muTil (i+1) times a power of chiD with exponent −(R.N (i+1))/2, and rhoDet' as muTil (i+1) times a power of chiD with exponent (R.N i)/2. Nothing is proved here, since the structure only lists what such a bundle must contain.

parts.name: R
parts.gloss: An object of the record type Ranks. The dossier shows that this holds natural numbers k, m, t with k and m even, t odd, 2 ≤ m, m + 3 ≤ k, k + m − 1 + 5 ≤ t, 3·m < t and further inequalities, on top of an unopened record Formalism.HC.Frame.

parts.name: host
parts.gloss: An object of the record type Host R. The dossier shows that it extends an unopened record Formalism.HC.HostAx and adds, among much else, an embedding φ₀ of the field E into ℂ, a finite set levelPrimes, two distinct primes g 0 and g 1 in that set, and two distinct primes pde and pde' that are 1 modulo 15.

parts.name: sp
parts.gloss: An object of the record type Spaces, built for R, the fields host.F and host.E and the star operation host.cmStar. The dossier shows that it holds a prime T and families X, Y, W, V of objects of type HSpace host.E, which are finite-dimensional spaces with a nondegenerate Hermitian form hT and a lattice L0, plus linear maps and rank conditions between them.

parts.name: vol
parts.gloss: A function that gives a real number to every object of type HSpace host.E.

parts.name: vol_pos
parts.gloss: The condition that vol W is greater than 0 for every W.

parts.name: what₂
parts.gloss: An object of the record type Rows.Data R. The dossier shows that it holds a field LL with a ring map embLL into ℂ, a places record, a ring O with a map OtoLL into LL, a finite type Tau with R.f elements, a type Tup with marked elements mu0, muStar, muStar', a type Word, finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces EE, Amb μ and Mu u, and functions perCol and Bu.

parts.name: eTau
parts.gloss: A bijection between the type what₂.Tau and the set that the code calls R.Psi.

parts.name: hc
parts.gloss: A function that gives to each τ in Tau an object of type HCParam R. The dossier shows that such an object holds rational sequences u, v, b, e with interlacing and gap inequalities, with u taking half-integer values and v, b, e taking integer values.

parts.name: wordFin
parts.gloss: The requirement that the type what₂.Word is finite, given as an instance.

parts.name: u₀
parts.gloss: A chosen element of what₂.Word, used below as the base word.

parts.name: hcW
parts.gloss: A function that gives an object of type HCParam R to each word u and each τ in Tau.

parts.name: hcW_base
parts.gloss: The condition that hcW at the base word u₀ equals hc.

parts.name: hcW_v
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and τ the v-component of hcW u τ equals the v-component of hc τ.

parts.name: hcW_b
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and τ the b-component of hcW u τ equals the b-component of hc τ.

parts.name: hcW_e
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and τ the e-component of hcW u τ equals the e-component of hc τ.

parts.name: hcW_first
parts.gloss: The condition that, when 0 < R.k, the entry of index 0 of the u-component of hcW u τ equals that of hc τ, for all u and τ.

parts.name: hcW_last
parts.gloss: The condition that, when 0 < R.k, the entry of index R.k − 1 of the u-component of hcW u τ equals that of hc τ, for all u and τ.

parts.name: mem
parts.gloss: A function that gives to each word u an object of type Member R what₂.Tau (hcW u). The dossier shows that a member is a triple of a column chain C, an object A of the unopened type ColumnsAtT R C, and a period map P.

parts.name: nfLL
parts.gloss: The requirement that what₂.LL is a number field, given as an instance.

parts.name: starLL
parts.gloss: A star operation on what₂.LL, that is an involution compatible with the ring structure, given as an instance.

parts.name: tcLL
parts.gloss: The requirement that the number field what₂.LL is totally complex, given as an instance.

parts.name: galLL
parts.gloss: The requirement that what₂.LL is a Galois extension of ℚ, given as an instance.

parts.name: starLL_cx
parts.gloss: The condition that embLL carries the star of x to the complex conjugate of embLL x, for every x in LL.

parts.name: div
parts.gloss: An object of the record type DivData what₂.LL what₂.Word. The dossier shows that it holds an object RR and a family Nu u of the unopened type HLat, linear maps Bk, real numbers h u, HH, etaF and delP with delP ≤ 1, a natural number Dall, and one inequality on HH.

parts.name: div_good
parts.gloss: A conjunction of two conditions. The matrix (div.RR.X v) has invertible determinant for every v, and the matrix ((div.Nu u).X v) has invertible determinant for all u and v.

parts.name: embE
parts.gloss: A ring homomorphism from the field host.E into what₂.LL.

parts.name: embE_φ₀
parts.gloss: The condition that embLL composed with embE equals the embedding host.φ₀ of host.E into ℂ.

parts.name: conjF
parts.gloss: An algebra homomorphism from host.E to itself over host.F.

parts.name: conjF_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that conjF x equals host.conj x for every x.

parts.name: embE_conj
parts.gloss: The condition that embE carries host.conj x to the star of embE x, for every x in host.E.

parts.name: LL0
parts.gloss: An intermediate field between ℚ and what₂.LL.

parts.name: hostField_le_fixedField
parts.gloss: The condition that embE x lies in LL0 for every x in host.E.

parts.name: O_int
parts.gloss: The condition that the image in LL of every element of the ring what₂.O is integral over ℤ.

parts.name: O_contains
parts.gloss: The condition that for every x in the ring of integers of host.E there is a y in what₂.O whose image in LL equals embE x.

parts.name: plEq
parts.gloss: A bijection between the type what₂.places.Pl and the set of nonzero prime ideals of the ring of integers of what₂.LL (written HeightOneSpectrum).

parts.name: val_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that for every w and every nonzero x in LL the value what₂.places.val w x equals vAdd (plEq w) x. The dossier shows vAdd to be minus the logarithm of the valuation at that prime, an integer.

parts.name: ram_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that what₂.places.ramIdx w equals eWL of plEq w for every w. The dossier shows eWL to be the ramification index of that prime ideal over ℤ.

parts.name: conj_val
parts.gloss: The condition that the value of x at the place what₂.places.conj w equals the value of star x at w, for all w and x.

parts.name: T_level
parts.gloss: The condition that the number (mem u).A.T lies in the finite set host.levelPrimes for every word u.

parts.name: T_norm
parts.gloss: The condition that for every word u there is an integer π of host.E that lies in host.K, satisfies π · host.conj π = (mem u).A.T, and has π − 1 in the ideal generated by the natural number host.QS · host.q · host.d · (host.g 0 · host.g 1)^2.

parts.name: sp_T
parts.gloss: The condition that the prime sp.T of the spaces record equals (mem u₀).A.T, the number attached to the member at the base word.

parts.name: cOf
parts.gloss: A function from words to elements of host.E.

parts.name: cOf_ne
parts.gloss: The condition that cOf u is nonzero for every u.

parts.name: cOf_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that cOf u · host.conj (cOf u) · (mem u).A.T equals (mem u₀).A.T in host.E, for every u.

parts.name: T_win
parts.gloss: The condition that for every u the real number (mem u).A.Tstar is at most (mem u).A.T, and (mem u).A.T is at most (1 + 1/(R.f · R.k)) · (mem u).A.Tstar.

parts.name: GamP_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that (mem u).A.GamP equals (mem u₀).A.GamP for every u.

parts.name: T_ne_pde
parts.gloss: The condition that (mem u).A.T differs from host.pde and from host.pde' for every u.

parts.name: Dstar_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that (mem u).A.Dstar equals the real number what₂.Dstar for every u.

parts.name: clsLat
parts.gloss: A function that gives, for each word u, index i and element c of (mem u).C.cls i, a submodule over the ring of integers of host.E inside the space (sp.X i).V.

parts.name: clsLat_lat
parts.gloss: The condition that each clsLat u i c is a full lattice over host.E, in the sense of the library predicate Submodule.IsFullLattice.

parts.name: eMu
parts.gloss: For each word u, a complex linear isomorphism from the space what₂.Mu u onto (mem u).A.Mram.

parts.name: eMt
parts.gloss: For each word u, a complex linear isomorphism from (mem u).P.Mt onto the space what₂.Amb what₂.mu0.

parts.name: perCol_base_eq_PtilCol
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u, φ in Mu u and F in Amb mu0, the number what₂.perCol u mu0 φ F equals (mem u).P.PtilCol applied to the image of φ under eMu u, read as a function on cls 0 and Y 0, and to the preimage of F under eMt u.

parts.name: Bu_linL
parts.gloss: The condition that what₂.Bu u φ F is complex linear in φ for every u and every fixed F.

parts.name: Bu_linR
parts.gloss: The condition that what₂.Bu u φ F is complex linear in F for every u and every fixed φ.

parts.name: chTw
parts.gloss: A function that gives, for each word u and each element of what₂.Tup, an object of type ColumnChain R what₂.Tau (hcW u). The dossier shows that a column chain holds finite types cls i, finite groups stab i c, types Y i, complex numbers rhoDet and rhoDet' of absolute value 1 below index R.m, and linear maps unf.

parts.name: memberColumns_twistedChain_base
parts.gloss: The condition that chTw u at the tuple mu0 equals the column chain (mem u).C, for every u.

parts.name: e0Tw
parts.gloss: For all u and μ, a complex linear isomorphism from the functions cls 0 → Y 0 → ℂ of the chain (mem u).C onto the same kind of function space of the chain chTw u μ.

parts.name: PTw
parts.gloss: For all u and μ, an object of type PeriodMap R (chTw u μ). The dossier shows that a period map holds complex vector spaces Mt, Wz, Wrow and linear maps evz, lowerMap and period.

parts.name: eMtTw
parts.gloss: For all u and μ, a complex linear isomorphism from (PTw u μ).Mt onto what₂.Amb μ.

parts.name: perCol_tie
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and all μ different from mu0, and all φ and F, the number what₂.perCol u μ φ F equals (PTw u μ).PtilCol applied to e0Tw u μ of the image of φ under eMu u, and to the preimage of F under eMtTw u μ.

parts.name: jEE
parts.gloss: A map from div.RR.V into what₂.EE that is additive and semilinear along embLL, meaning that scalars from LL act on the target through embLL.

parts.name: jEE_basis
parts.gloss: The condition that the images under jEE of the vectors div.RR.b i are linearly independent over ℂ and span all of EE.

parts.name: jN
parts.gloss: For each u, a map from (div.Nu u).V into what₂.Mu u that is semilinear along embLL.

parts.name: jN_basis
parts.gloss: The condition that for each u the images under jN u of the vectors (div.Nu u).b i are linearly independent over ℂ and span all of Mu u.

parts.name: Dall_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that the natural number div.Dall equals what₂.Dall.

parts.name: delP_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that the real number div.delP equals what₂.delp.

parts.name: Dt
parts.gloss: A type, with no further description at this point.

parts.name: instDt
parts.gloss: A commutative group structure on Dt, given as an instance.

parts.name: detCls
parts.gloss: A function that gives an element of Dt to each u, i and element of (mem u).C.cls i.

parts.name: muTil
parts.gloss: For each natural number, a group homomorphism from Dt to the nonzero complex numbers.

parts.name: chiD
parts.gloss: A group homomorphism from Dt to the nonzero complex numbers.

parts.name: UO
parts.gloss: A subgroup of Dt.

parts.name: chiD_UO
parts.gloss: The condition that chiD takes the value 1 on every element of UO.

parts.name: e1Dt
parts.gloss: A group homomorphism into Dt from the unitary elements of host.E, that is the elements whose product with their star is 1.

parts.name: rest_detCharacter_on_unitary_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that for every unitary z in host.E the complex number chiD (e1Dt z) equals the product over τ in Tau of the inverse of host.emb (eTau τ) z.

parts.name: relDet
parts.gloss: A function that gives, for each N and each pair of objects of type SDLat host.E N, an element of the quotient group Dt / UO. The dossier shows SDLat E N to be the submodules of E^N over the integers of E that satisfy an unopened condition IsSDLat.

parts.name: relDet_self
parts.gloss: The condition that relDet N L L equals 1 for all N and L.

parts.name: relDet_mul
parts.gloss: The condition that relDet N L L' · relDet N L' L'' equals relDet N L L'' for all N, L, L', L''.

parts.name: relDet_smul
parts.gloss: The condition that whenever L' is the image of L under a unitary N by N matrix γ over host.E, relDet N L L' equals the class in Dt / UO of e1Dt applied to the determinant of γ.

parts.name: rhoDet_eq_inv_muTilde_chiD_pow
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u, i and c in (mem u).C.cls i, the number (mem u).C.rhoDet i c equals the inverse of muTil (i+1) (detCls u i c) times chiD (detCls u i c) raised to the power −((R.N (i+1))/2), with the division taken in the natural numbers.

parts.name: rhoDetPrime_eq_muTilde_mul_chi_pow
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u, i and c in (mem u).C.cls (i+1), the number (mem u).C.rhoDet' i c equals muTil (i+1) (detCls u (i+1) c) times chiD (detCls u (i+1) c) raised to the power (R.N i)/2, with the division taken in the natural numbers.

parts.name: dsig
parts.gloss: A function from what₂.Tau to the real numbers.

parts.name: dsig_pos
parts.gloss: The condition that dsig ρ is greater than 0 for every ρ.

parts.name: s
parts.gloss: An object of the type that the code calls Formalism.MainNotions.S.Draft.SData, built for R, host.F, host.E, conjF, the words, Tau and hcW. Its body is not in the dossier.

parts.name: s_split
parts.gloss: The condition that for every p the optional value (s.atP p).split is present exactly when the number that the code calls Loc.resChar p is one of the two primes host.g 0 and host.g 1.

parts.name: s_HH
parts.gloss: The condition that the complex dimension of the space s.HH equals what₂.Dall.

parts.name: s_Cu
parts.gloss: For each u, a complex linear isomorphism from s.Cu u onto (mem u).A.Mu0.

parts.name: s_PlF
parts.gloss: A bijection between s.PlF and the set of nonzero prime ideals of the ring of integers of host.F.

parts.name: loc
parts.gloss: An object of type LocTheory. The dossier shows this to be a choice, for every prime l, of an object of the unopened type LocPrime l.

parts.name: locA
parts.gloss: For every prime l, an object of type LocAinf l (loc l). The dossier shows that this holds group actions actC and actT, a sequence ζ n with ζ 0 = 1, ζ (n+1)^l = ζ n and ζ 1 ≠ 1, an element ε, and an injective ring map ιA from Ainf l into the ring (loc l).R.B with compatibility conditions.

parts.name: locT
parts.gloss: For every prime l, an object of type LocTied l (loc l) (locA l). The dossier shows that this holds ring isomorphisms eB and eD from the rings (loc l).R.B and (loc l).R.BdR onto rings that the code calls Per.Bcris l and Per.BdR l, with conditions that they respect the group actions, a map φB, filtrations and the map ιA.

parts.name: nd
parts.gloss: An object of type NData R host what₂. The visible part of its body holds an algebraic closure Om of host.E, an index type Loc with a prime l i, an index j i between 1 and R.m, a place w i, complete discrete valuation rings O i that are finite over the l i-adic integers, finite sets X i, modules Mt i and characters chi i c.

parts.name: ntw
parts.gloss: An object of type NTw R host what₂ LL0 nd. The visible part of its body holds a ring automorphism cc of nd.Om, an index type Tw with primes l i, discrete valuation rings O0 i, O i and Ok i k, embeddings of LL0, and characters delta i whose inertia images have exactly 15 elements at the places in pD i.

parts.name: naut
parts.gloss: An object of type NAut nd. The visible part of its body holds field maps iotaQ and iotaQC, and for each place w a type LP w with a dimension lpDim, a sum lpSum, a twist lpTw, predicates unr, mono0 and tempered, a multiset frobEig, and laws relating them.

parts.name: nbc
parts.gloss: An object of type NBC naut. The dossier shows that it holds types AU j and Wt j with multisets satAU of size R.nV / 2 and infW of size R.nV, and injective maps embAV from naut.AV i into AU (nd.j i) that respect the local data.

parts.name: nexp
parts.gloss: An object of type NExp R host what₂ LL0 nd ntw. The visible part of its body holds finite-dimensional spaces Fm i j b with an action of the group G0g nd, central idempotents eAlg i b in a group algebra, a function eLL0 from G0g nd to LL0, and homomorphisms delU with conditions.

parts.name: ntypes
parts.gloss: An object of type NTypes naut. The visible part of its body holds a number field Mray that is Galois with commutative Galois group over host.K, multisets bc σ of pairs with the products summing to R.r, homomorphisms rbar into GL of size R.r, elements tg k v of inertia groups, and central orthogonal idempotents eSer.

parts.name: nStage_trivialCharacter_compat
parts.gloss: A condition that the code calls ntypes.IdempotentMatchesAction. Its body is not visible in the dossier.

parts.name: nStage_trivialCharacter_coeff_eq
parts.gloss: The condition that for every g in G0g nd the image under embLL of nexp.eLL0 g equals the coefficient at g of ntypes.e0. The dossier shows G0g nd to be the families of invertible R.r by R.r matrices over the integers modulo host.g k, indexed by pairs of k in {0, 1} and an element of nd.PlG k.

parts.name: nth
parts.gloss: An object of type NTh R host what₂ LL0 nd ntw nexp. The visible part of its body holds ring maps iC into the l-adic complex numbers, numbers aL i equal to 1 when ntw.l i is one of host.g k and 0 otherwise, injective evaluation maps ev, polynomial sets Harm cut out by second-order differential conditions, and maps thV, recDet and actK.

parts.name: nbr
parts.gloss: For each i in nd.Loc and each prime w of host.E containing nd.l i, an object of type LocBridge. The dossier shows that this holds a field map j from nd.Om into Om l, a group isomorphism e that is continuous in both directions from the group that the code calls Dec at w onto GK Kw, and a ring isomorphism eO from nd.O i onto OL LL.

parts.name: nbr_ind
parts.gloss: The condition that for all such i and w an element x of nd.Om lies in nd.plOm.1 w exactly when the norm of its image under the map j of nbr i w is at most 1.

parts.name: self_good
parts.gloss: The condition GoodCoef host.condN on the field LL of each bridge nbr i w. The dossier shows GoodCoef N LL to say that every x in Om l with x raised to the least common multiple of l and N equal to 1 lies in LL.

parts.name: ntwbr
parts.gloss: For each i in ntw.Tw and each prime w of host.E containing ntw.l i, an object of type LocBridge of the same kind as nbr, now with the ring ntw.O0 i.

parts.name: ntwbr_ind
parts.gloss: The condition that for all such i and w an element x of nd.Om lies in nd.plOm.1 w exactly when the norm of its image under the map j of ntwbr i w is at most 1.

parts.name: loc_tie
parts.gloss: The condition LocTie nd naut loc nbr. The dossier shows that it asks, for every i and w, that a map iotaOQ agrees with the bridge map toLL, and that the predicates IsCrysW, IsdRW, IsPotCrysW and the multiset jumpsW of naut agree with the corresponding predicates and multiplicities of the bridge computed in loc, for continuous matrix representations over nd.O i and over larger fields LL'.

parts.name: bc_tie
parts.gloss: The condition BcTie nd naut ntypes. The dossier shows that it asks that whenever a list Sig satisfies the unopened condition HasParamW and two further conditions on its entries, the multiset ntypes.bc σ equals the multiset of pairs (a, d) read off from Sig.

parts.name: rbar_tie
parts.gloss: The condition RbarTie nd naut ntypes. The dossier shows that it asks, under the unopened conditions HasParamW and IsRepOfSig, that ntypes.rbar σ (nd.w i) satisfies the unopened condition IsSSRep and has, for every group element, the same characteristic polynomial as the reduction of ρ modulo the maximal ideal of nd.O i, after moving both to a common field.

parts.name: mtpar_tie
parts.gloss: The condition MtParTie nd naut ntypes. The dossier shows that it asks that ntypes.MtPar (nd.mu i) (nd.j i) σ' equals the supremum of the submodules naut.typeV i P over those P that satisfy a condition built from the unopened names isoLoc, IsBCV, twistIso and muPart.

parts.name: Z_tie
parts.gloss: The condition that for all i the finite set nd.Z i has the same elements as the set ZN nd naut i. The dossier shows ZN to be the set of x that arise as naut.ptV i P for some P that satisfies the unopened condition IsBCV with a parameter list containing one named entry.

parts.name: Zgood_tie
parts.gloss: The condition that for all i the finite set nd.Zgood i has the same elements as ZgoodN nd naut i. The dossier shows ZgoodN to be the elements x of ZN for which some Sig satisfies the unopened conditions HasParamX and goodSig.

parts.name: etaJ_tie
parts.gloss: The condition that for all j with 1 ≤ j ≤ R.m and all w, the quantity what₂.etaJ j w equals the sum of nd.etaLoc i over i in the finite set nd.locs j w. The dossier shows that nd.locs j w consists of the i with nd.j i = j and nd.w i = w.

parts.name: fm
parts.gloss: For each word u, an object of type MemberForms built for what₂.LL, embLL, the places record, Tau, hcW u and the three components of mem u. The visible part of its body holds modules lv and lk of rank R.N i, maps dil with a group-action law, weights lam, subspaces Fi with Fi 0 = A.Mu0, forms ipV, objects lat i of type HLat and semilinear maps emb i.

parts.name: eMu_isom
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and all φ, ψ in what₂.Mu u, the inner product of φ and ψ equals (fm u).ipC 0 applied to their images under eMu u, read as functions on cls 0 and Y 0.

parts.name: nuIn
parts.gloss: For each u, a linear map over what₂.LL from (div.Nu u).V into ((fm u).lat 0).V.

parts.name: nuIn_inj
parts.gloss: The condition that nuIn u is injective for every u.

parts.name: nuIn_range
parts.gloss: The condition that the image of nuIn u equals the submodule (fm u).ramSub for every u.

parts.name: nuIn_jN
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and x the image of jN u x under eMu u, read as a function on cls 0 and Y 0, equals (fm u).emb 0 applied to nuIn u x.

parts.name: nuIn_norm
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u, v and x the real number normAt computed in (div.Nu u) at v on x equals normAt computed in (fm u).lat 0 at v on nuIn u x. The dossier shows normAt to be cnorm of fcoord, two names it does not open.

parts.name: jEE_norm
parts.gloss: The condition that for every x in div.RR.V the number normAt of x in div.RR, taken at the infinite place given by embLL, equals the norm of jEE x in EE.

parts.name: s_Cu_isom
parts.gloss: The condition that for all u and all x, y in s.Cu u, the inner product of x and y equals (fm u).ipC 0 applied to their images under s_Cu u, read as functions on cls 0 and Y 0.

parts.name: sEE
parts.gloss: A map from what₂.EE to s.HH that preserves norms and is conjugate-linear over ℂ, as the starred arrow in the Lean text indicates.

parts.name: cd
parts.gloss: An object of type CDHaar. The dossier shows that it holds, for all natural numbers P and Q, a Haar measure on a space that the code calls UpqT P Q, that the measure for (N, 0) is a probability measure, and that for all P and Q some constant c, neither 0 nor infinite, satisfies the unopened condition OmegaDensity for both (P, Q) and (P + Q, 0).

parts.name: jet
parts.gloss: An object of type ThetaJet R host. The dossier shows that it holds index types Sit and Sit1, local objects loc i and loc1 i of the unopened types JetLoc and JetLoc1, indices jOf i and j1Of i between 1 and R.m, and conditions that the numbers N0 and N1 of each local object equal R.N at the index minus one and at the index.

parts.name: jetU
parts.gloss: A function from jet.Sit to the words of what₂.

parts.name: jetL
parts.gloss: For each i in jet.Sit, an element of the class set (mem (jetU i)).C.cls (jet.jOf i − 1).

parts.name: jetL'
parts.gloss: For each i in jet.Sit, an element of the class set (mem (jetU i)).C.cls (jet.jOf i).

parts.name: jetW
parts.gloss: A function from jet.Sit to what₂.places.Pl.

parts.name: jetW_l
parts.gloss: The condition that what₂.places.resChar (jetW i) equals the number (jet.loc i).l for every i.

parts.name: jetTau
parts.gloss: For each i in jet.Sit, a function from the integers modulo (jet.loc i).d to what₂.Tau.

parts.name: jetW1
parts.gloss: A function from jet.Sit1 to what₂.places.Pl.

parts.name: resChar_thetaJetPlaceDegOne
parts.gloss: The condition that what₂.places.resChar (jetW1 i) equals the number (jet.loc1 i).l for every i in jet.Sit1.

parts.name: jetTau1
parts.gloss: A function from jet.Sit1 to what₂.Tau.

parts.name: jetU1
parts.gloss: A function from jet.Sit1 to the words of what₂.

parts.name: jetL1
parts.gloss: For each i in jet.Sit1, an element of the class set (mem (jetU1 i)).C.cls (jet.j1Of i − 1).

parts.name: jetL1'
parts.gloss: For each i in jet.Sit1, an element of the class set (mem (jetU1 i)).C.cls (jet.j1Of i).

parts.name: gx
parts.gloss: An object of type GlobalExtra what₂.LL what₂.Tau. The dossier shows that it holds a positive real number Om τ s for each τ and each embedding s of LL into ℂ, and a positive real number thOne s for each such embedding.

parts.name: gat
parts.gloss: For each word u and place w such that GIdx host (mem u).A.T p holds for p = what₂.places.resChar w, an object of type GAtP p. The dossier shows GIdx to say that p is prime, 5 ≤ p, host.cls p is the value inertClass, the unopened condition HNeZero host p holds, p is not in host.levelPrimes and p does not divide T. It shows GAtP p to hold a discrete valuation ring O, a field Kf, a finite type comp with levels, and a number e.

parts.name: gat_d
parts.gloss: The condition that the number (gat u w h).d equals the complex dimension of (mem u).A.Mu0, for all u, w and h. The field d is not among the fields of GAtP that the dossier shows.

parts.name: Y_sigval
parts.gloss: The condition that for every j ≤ R.m and every embedding τ of host.E into ℂ, the pair (sp.Y j).sig τ equals sigYD R j. The dossier shows sigYD R j to be the pair (R.rankY j − (R.m − j)/2, (R.m − j)/2) of natural numbers.

unopened: Formalism.HC.Frame (and R.f, R.N, R.Psi, R.GG, R.r, R.nV, R.rankY, R.sigW, R.ord)
Formalism.HC.HostAx and its raw part (host.F, host.E, host.K, host.conj, host.cmStar, host.emb, host.gal, host.cls, host.QS, host.q, host.d, host.condN)
ColumnsAtT (and A.T, A.Tstar, A.GamP, A.Dstar, A.Mram, A.Mu0)
the cut tail of Rows.Data (including etaJ and shaLen)
FinExt, Om, GQ, GK, OL, Ainf, OC, OCb, PadicComplex, Qbar
Per.Bcris, Per.BdR, Per.IsCrisDR, Per.IsLog and the other Per names
the cut tails of NData, NTw, NAut, NExp, NTh, NTypes and MemberForms (including etaLoc, PlG, AV, ptV, typeV, ipC, ramSub)
HasParamW, HasParamX, goodSig, IsRepOfSig, IsSSRep, IsBCV, isoLoc, twistIso, muPart, iotaOQ, mapRep
LocBridge.IsCrysW, IsdRW, IsPotCrysW, IsJumpW, multW and their E variants
Formalism.MainNotions.G.Places, Level, and the field d of GAtP
glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names point to a global arithmetic setup around a CM field E over a totally real field F, with Hermitian spaces and unitary groups, a tower of automorphic forms on class sets linked by theta-type period maps, Galois representations with crystalline and de Rham conditions tied to p-adic period rings, and Hecke data at auxiliary primes. The name D7 and the module name suggest that this is the seventh layer of a staged data package whose newest addition is the pair of determinant-character formulas for rhoDet and rhoDet'.
glossary.why: The whole text of D7 and the bodies of most level-one records are visible, but several of those bodies are cut off and many conditions rest on names from deeper levels (such as ColumnsAtT, HostAx, Frame, Places, HLat and SData) that the dossier does not open.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.S0.UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses
glossary.what: a record type whose 60 fields are all propositions, so it is itself a proposition (a bundle of hypotheses)
glossary.says: This is a structure in Prop with 60 fields, and each field is a proof of one named proposition. It therefore states the conjunction of those 60 propositions, with no parameters and no quantifiers of its own. Fifty-six of the fields are single named statements, most of them in a namespace called Published, and the dossier shows a body for each of these, although most bodies rest on conditions that are not opened. Three fields (litN, toHypothesesX, nLink) are themselves smaller bundles, and one field (siegelEisensteinSimplePole) has a type that unfolds to True and so asserts nothing. Several statements occur more than once, directly and again inside the sub-bundles.

parts.name: clozelCohomological
parts.gloss: For every totally complex number field E, every natural number a with 1 ≤ a, and every π of the type the code calls CuspSub E a, if CG.mk π satisfies the condition called IsRegAlg then π satisfies the condition called GKCoh.IsCohomological. Those two conditions are not opened.

parts.name: greenCuspidal
parts.gloss: A proof of the proposition that the code calls GlobalTheory.GLq.Green. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: heckeLAdicCharacter
parts.gloss: For every number field E with algebraic closure Ω there is a group homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω that satisfies IsGlobalArtin, and such that for every prime l, every ring isomorphism ι from Qbar l to the complex numbers, every χ of type HChar E and every integer-valued function n on the embeddings of E into ℂ with IsAlgPos χ n, there is exactly one continuous homomorphism r from G E Ω to the units of Qbar l with IsLAdicOf art ι χ n r. The named conditions are not opened.

parts.name: chebotarevDegreeOne
parts.gloss: For a number field F with algebraic closure Ω, a finite Galois intermediate field L, an automorphism g of L over F and a finite set S of nonzero primes of the ring of integers of F, there is a prime v outside S with inertia degree 1 over ℤ, together with a valuation subring B of Ω with IsPlaceOver B v whose group Ine B lies in the subgroup fixing L, and an element σ of G F Ω with IsFrob B (normV v) σ whose restriction to L is g. IsPlaceOver, Ine and IsFrob are not opened.

parts.name: galoisRepOfPolarizedCuspidal
parts.gloss: The proposition UpperTheory.GalS.CuspUAlt. For every field E carrying the unopened class IsCMField, algebraic closure Ω, prime l, isomorphism ι from Qbar l to ℂ, a ≥ 1, π in CuspSub E a and χ in HChar of the maximal real subfield of E, if CG.mk π is IsRegAlg and IsPolarized π χ holds, then there exist a homomorphism r from G E Ω to GL of size a over Qbar l, an integer wt and a function HT from embeddings of E into Qbar l to multisets of integers with the unopened condition IsGalUAlt π χ ι r wt HT.

parts.name: baseChangeDefiniteUnitary
parts.gloss: An abbreviation for UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.DefiniteN. For every IsCMField E in which every prime w satisfies Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt over the integers of the maximal real subfield, every n ≥ 1 and every submodule π of complex functions on UA E n with IsAutRepU π, there exist a number c, sizes N i summing to n, submodules V i of Sm E (N i), local objects σ and multisets m with the unopened condition IsBaseChangeU π h V σ m.

parts.name: bhattScholzeCrystallineLattices
parts.gloss: For a prime l, K in FinExt l (a finite-dimensional intermediate field over the l-adic numbers), and data P₀, e with IsAinf K P₀ e, a conjunction of two statements holds. The first says that under IsStd P AI every lattice T with IsCrys admits an object E of type FCrys and a semilinear map j satisfying Realises, and the second says that any linear map f commuting with the two actions between two realised modules comes from exactly one u of type FHom E E' compatible with j and j'. IsAinf, IsStd, IsCrys, Realises and FCrys are not opened.

parts.name: heckeLAdicCharacterAbove
parts.gloss: A proof of the proposition that the code calls GlobalTheory.TripleGal.CharAbove. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: cuspRapidDecay
parts.gloss: For every D of type D7, every family θ with IsInfFam θ, every V of type HSp D with e satisfying IsExpFam, and every complex function φ on GA D V satisfying IsAutFun, IsSmoothInf, IsUnifModerate and IsCuspFun, the condition CuspDecay.IsRapidDecay θ V φ holds. All of these conditions are unopened.

parts.name: weilSiegelFormulaUnitary
parts.gloss: For D of type D7, A and B of type HSp D, a Haar measure m on GA D B, 1 ≤ A.rank, and either wittIdx B = 0 or A.rank + wittIdx B < B.rank, two things hold. First, a seminorm ν with IsContSeminorm bounds absThetaInt. Second, for every ω with IsWeilDatumO ψ (dblSp A) B 1 χ ω and every f with IsThetaFunO, a descended function is integrable and, when 2 * A.rank < B.rank, a coset sum over siegel A in GQ (dblSp A) of the section swSection converges in the sense CosetConv and equals the average of that descended function. The named objects are unopened.

parts.name: siegelWeilUnitaryConvergent
parts.gloss: For D of type D7 and A, B of type HSp D with A.rank < B.rank, B.rank ≤ 2 * A.rank and A.rank + wittIdx B < B.rank, and under a list of unopened conditions (IsWeilDatumO, IsMaj, HasIwasawa, IsInfFam, IsCartanInv, a commutation condition, IsCovolOne, Haar measure, IsFockVec), a descended function built from thetaKO is integrable for every g, and the unopened relation Eis.EisValueAt holds between a section at the point sZero A B and thetaMean ω ν f.

parts.name: doublingMethod
parts.gloss: An abbreviation for the proposition that the code calls ResidueKilled.DM. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: unramifiedDoublingGL
parts.gloss: For a nonarchimedean local field k of characteristic zero, a Haar measure μ on GL of size n over k giving the subgroup KO measure 1, a representation π with HasSatake π α and a function ω with IsZonal, there is a real s₀ such that for every complex s with real part above s₀ the function sphSection times ω is integrable and its integral equals lFactor (resCard k) α (s + 1/2) times lFactor (resCard k) α⁻¹ (s + 1/2) times invNormFactor (resCard k) n s. HasSatake, IsZonal, sphSection, lFactor and invNormFactor are unopened.

parts.name: bernsteinZelevinskyFiniteness
parts.gloss: For every nonarchimedean local field k, the conjunction of four statements called IrreducibleAdmissible, JacquetFiniteLength, InductionFiniteLength and InductionContragredient. Their bodies are shown and say that smooth irreducible complex representations of GL n k are IsAdmissible, that jac and parInd preserve HasFiniteLength for smooth representations, and that there is an equivalence between parInd of contra ρ and contra of parInd ρ given by an integral over KO, where IsAdmissible, HasFiniteLength, jac, parInd and contra are unopened.

parts.name: formalDegreeCompactDual
parts.gloss: For cd of type CDHaar and scale factors sc n ε that make the scaled measures muG match cd under every reindexing, and for every strictly decreasing lam with lam a − (N − 1)/2 an integer, every σ with the unopened condition IsDS ε lam σ and every nonzero w, the quotient of ‖w‖ to the power 4 by the integral of the squared absolute value of the inner product of w with σ(g)w equals the product over a < b of |lam a − lam b| divided by the product over a < b of (b − a).

parts.name: bernsteinUnitaryProductIrreducible
parts.gloss: For a nonarchimedean local field k and complex representations π₁ of GL r k and π₂ of GL t k that are each smooth (every vector has open stabiliser), irreducible and unitarisable (they preserve a positive definite Hermitian form), the representation prod₂ π₁ π₂ is irreducible. The body of prod₂ is shown as ind₂ applied to extTensor π₁ π₂, and ind₂ and extTensor are unopened.

parts.name: geometricLemmaFiltration
parts.gloss: For every nonarchimedean local field k, the condition that the code calls GlobalTheory.SmGL.JacquetOfInducedFiltration k. That condition is not opened.

parts.name: unlinkedProductIrreducible
parts.gloss: For π₁ in Irr k r and π₂ in Irr k t with IsCuspSupport data σ and σ', if no σ a is equivalent to a twist of any σ' b of the same size by detChar of unrChar k α for a nonzero complex α, then prod₂ π₁.π π₂.π is irreducible. Irr, IsCuspSupport, twist, detChar and unrChar are unopened.

parts.name: depthZeroJacquetInjective
parts.gloss: For π in Irr k n and a vector v fixed by the join of KOne k with the intersection of unipRad k e and KO k, if the class of v in the quotient Jacquet π.π (unipRad k e) is zero then v is zero. KOne, KO, unipRad and Jacquet are unopened.

parts.name: jacquetShalika
parts.gloss: The conjunction of two propositions that the code calls JacquetShalikaRigidity and JacquetShalikaBound. Neither body is shown.

parts.name: automorphicFormsFiniteGL
parts.gloss: For a totally complex number field E, an open subgroup L of GL of size a over the finite adele ring of E, a finite-dimensional complex representation ρ of Kinf E a (a unitary matrix group over Cinf E) whose matrix coefficients are continuous, and any function c, the complex span of the set forms L ρ c is finite-dimensional. The set forms is shown as those φ with IsAutForm that are fixed by L, have coefficients in AutFin.coeffSpan ρ and satisfy cap τ u φ = c τ u • φ, where these inner names are unopened.

parts.name: localGlobalAboveL
parts.gloss: The proposition UpperTheory.GalS.CarUAlt. For an IsCMField E, a prime l, an isomorphism ι, a ≥ 2 and π in CuspSub E a with π.IsCsd and CG.mk π IsRegAlg, there exist r, wt and HT with IsGalUAlt π (quadChar E ^ a) ι r wt HT such that at every prime w in placesOver E l, for every σ with π.IsLocComp w σ and every rc with IsRecT h rc and NcW (rc (algNorm σ)), the relation Ab holds between wdAt of r restricted to the subgroup Dec A and rc (algNorm σ). All of these conditions are unopened.

parts.name: regularAlgebraicPurity
parts.gloss: For an IsCMField E, a ≥ 1 and π in CuspSub E a with CG.mk π IsRegAlg, there is an integer w₀ such that for every embedding τ of E into ℂ the multiset infChar at the complex conjugate of τ equals infChar at τ with each entry z replaced by w₀ − z, and also GKCoh.IsCohomological π holds.

parts.name: globalArtinReciprocity
parts.gloss: For every number field E with algebraic closure Ω there exists a group homomorphism art from Ideles E to Gab E Ω with the unopened condition IsGlobalArtin art.

parts.name: heckeLAdicParameterAbove
parts.gloss: The proposition HeckeLAdicParameterAboveAlt. For art with IsGlobalArtin, χ and n with IsAlgPos χ n, and a continuous μ with IsLAdicOf art ι χ n μ, at every prime w with local data A, Bw, ξ satisfying IsPlaceOver, Pst.Induces and NPin.IsComp χ w ξ, and every rc with IsRecT h rc, the object wdAt of (rk1 μ) restricted to Dec A equals rc applied to the class of Irr.ofDet 1 ξ. All these names are unopened.

parts.name: deRhamPotSemistable
