parts.gloss: For a prime l with P and AI such that LocTied l P AI is nonempty, K in FinExt l, and a finite-dimensional l-adic representation ρ of the subgroup GK K (the subgroup fixing K) with continuous orbit maps, the condition IsDR (P.PD K) ρ implies the condition IsPst P ρ. IsDR and IsPst are unopened.

parts.name: harishChandraFinite
parts.gloss: For D of type D7, θ with IsInfFam, V of type HSp D, an open subgroup U of GA D V, data ε and fr with IsFrameFam, finite-dimensional representations ρ τ with IsContRep, and any c, the complex span of the set forms θ V U ε fr ρ c is finite-dimensional. This set forms and the conditions are unopened.

parts.name: greenRegularCharacters
parts.gloss: For a prime g, d > 0 and a field K of dimension d over the integers mod g, there is a map τ from characters θ of the units of K to complex functions on Gn g d such that for θ with IsRegularChar the function τ θ is IsCusp, has value at 1 equal to the product over i from 1 to d − 1 of (g^i − 1), and at y with irreducible characteristic polynomial having a root z in K has value (−1)^(d−1) times the sum over i < d of θ(z^(g^i)). Also τ θ = τ θ' exactly when θ' = θ^(g^i) for some i < d, and every IsCusp function is τ θ for some regular θ, where Gn, IsRegularChar and IsCusp are unopened.

parts.name: zelevinskyPolynomialRing
parts.gloss: For every nonarchimedean local field k there exist a family Z assigning to each Δ of type Segment k an element of IrrCl of GL of size Δ.len * Δ.d, and an additive isomorphism Ψ from GrothGL k to the polynomial ring over ℤ in variables indexed by Segment k, with IsSegmentClass k Z, IsProductIso k Ψ and Ψ sending the generator of Z Δ to the variable X Δ. Segment, IrrCl, GrothGL and the two conditions are unopened.

parts.name: rayClassFieldSt
parts.gloss: A proof of the proposition that the code calls GlobalTheory.NT.RayField. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: rayCharacterArtin
parts.gloss: For a number field F, a nonzero ideal 𝔪 of its integers and a homomorphism f from idealsPrimeTo 𝔪 to a commutative group A that is trivial on principal ideals generated by x with x − 1 in 𝔪, there is a homomorphism φ from G F Ω to A with open kernel, trivial on Ine B at primes not dividing 𝔪, sending every σ with IsFrob at such a prime v to f of primeElt 𝔪 v, with a stated description of the image of Ine B at primes dividing 𝔪, and φ is the only open-kernel homomorphism with that Frobenius property.

parts.name: genericUnitaryDualGL
parts.gloss: For a nonarchimedean local field k of characteristic zero, every smooth, irreducible, unitarisable complex representation π of GL N k that satisfies IsGeneric also satisfies GenericUnitary.IsComplementaryProduct. Those last two conditions are unopened.

parts.name: standardCosocleGL
parts.gloss: For a nonarchimedean local field k of characteristic zero, a multiset 𝔪 of Segment k and a family x of h elements of IrrGL whose sizes sum to N with LFactors 𝔪 x, there exists π of type IrrRep (GL N k) with IsCosocle π.ρ (prodIrr x hd). LFactors, IsCosocle and prodIrr are unopened.

parts.name: cheb
parts.gloss: The proposition GlobalTheory.TwSys.Cheb. For a number field F, an open normal subgroup U of G F Ω, an element g and a finite set A of primes, there is a prime v outside A with inertia degree 1 and ramification index 1 over ℤ, a valuation subring B with IsPlaceOver B v and Ine B inside U, and σ with IsFrob B (normV v) σ and σ g⁻¹ in U.

parts.name: discreteSeriesCover
parts.gloss: For natural numbers p, q with 1 ≤ p + q and T of type GrpData p q, there is a map D from rational-valued functions lam on Ix p q with IsParam lam to DSRep T such that every D lam satisfies HasTypes (D lam) lam and every R in DSRep T satisfies UnitEquiv R (D lam) for some lam. These names are unopened.

parts.name: harishChandraModules
parts.gloss: The conjunction of two statements. The first is that HarishChandraModulesOn T holds for all p, q with 1 ≤ p + q and all T of type GrpData p q, and the second is the proposition called KFiniteAnalyticUJ, and neither inner name is opened.

parts.name: casselmanWallach
parts.gloss: For σ on a complex Hilbert space H with IsURepOn and IsIrredOn for UJset ε, a complete Hausdorff space E with seminorms p and maps π, dπ satisfying IsSmoothModRep, and a linear map T₀ with IsGKMap, there is a linear map T agreeing with T₀ on vectors with IsKFin, satisfying IsSmoothGMap, unique on the vectors with SmoothVec among such maps, with closed image of those vectors, and, if T₀ is nonzero on some IsKFin vector, with each sobNorm bounded by a continuous seminorm of T w. The named conditions are unopened.

parts.name: weilRepresentationUnitaryPair
parts.gloss: For D of type D7, an additive character ψ with IsStdChar D ψ (−1), S and T of type HSp D, and circle-valued characters χS, χT with IsHeckeChar and ResEta conditions for S.rank and T.rank, there exists a homomorphism ω from GA D S × GA D T to linear endomorphisms of the complex functions on WO S T with IsWeilDatumO ψ S T χS χT ω.

parts.name: discreteSeriesExists
parts.gloss: Defined to be the proposition that the code calls DiscreteSeriesUpqExists. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: discreteSeriesClassification
parts.gloss: For every n there is a family of inner product spaces H ε lam with maps π ε lam such that, for strictly decreasing lam with lam a − (n − 1)/2 an integer, the space is complete and nontrivial with IsURepOn, IsIrredOn, IsSqIntOn and HasInfChar, has a unique submodule with IsKTypeOf for lam + rhoN ε − rhoC ε, and every other IsKTypeOf parameter μ differs from that one by a natural-number combination of root a b with a < b. Conversely every complete nontrivial σ with those three conditions is carried, after a permutation s and for some such mu, by a linear isometry onto H (ε ∘ s) mu that intertwines the actions.

parts.name: strongApproxSU
parts.gloss: For number fields F, E with σ satisfying IsCMExt F E σ, M ≥ 2, J with IsHermND σ J and ε with IsPlacesIdem S₁ S₂ ε, if SUSupp σ J ε is not compact then every g in SUAdelic σ J lies in the closure of the set of products γ * h with γ in SURat σ J and h in SUSupp σ J ε. These names are unopened.

parts.name: siegelWeilUnitaryConvergent2
parts.gloss: A second statement with the same short name, from the namespace HeckeCharacterZeroLocus.SiegelWeilU. It says that for number fields F, E with IsCMExt F E σ and every M and J with IsHermND σ J, the unopened condition SiegelWeilAt F E σ M J holds.

parts.name: harishChandraAnalyticity
parts.gloss: The conjunction of two propositions that the code calls AdmissibleCoefficientsAnalytic and LeviSubmoduleDense. Neither body is shown.

parts.name: cuspTraceClass
parts.gloss: For D of type D7, V of type HSp D and a right-invariant Haar measure μ on GA D V, every f in CcGA V gives an operator RcuspOp V μ f satisfying IsTraceClass. These names are unopened.

parts.name: dixmierMalliavinFactorisation
parts.gloss: For a topological group G with a homomorphism ι into n by n complex matrices whose map to GL n ℂ is a closed embedding, a Haar measure μ, a neighbourhood V of the identity and f in CcMat ι, there are finitely many functions g i and h i in CcMat ι, with the support of g i inside V and the support of h i inside the support of f, such that f is the sum of conv μ (g i) (h i). CcMat and conv are unopened.

parts.name: flathFactorisation
parts.gloss: For IsCMExt F E σ, J with IsHermND σ J and a homomorphism π from GAd σ J to bounded operators on H with IsIrrUnitary π, there exist local objects R v of type IrrU (GPl σ J v), vectors ξ v and a map B with Flath.IsUnramFactorisation R ξ π B. These names are unopened.

parts.name: cMCurveGoodOutsidePrimeSt
parts.gloss: For every prime p with p mod 4 = 3 and 3 < p there exist a subfield F of ℂ that is a number field and a Weierstrass curve A over F with IsGoodCMCurve p F A and HasMinimalDiscriminant A (−p^3). Those two conditions are unopened.

parts.name: weberRayFieldSt
parts.gloss: For a totally complex number field K inside ℂ of degree 2 over ℚ with discriminant less than −4, a period pair L whose lattice is exactly the image of the ring of integers of K, and n > 0, the field obtained by adjoining weberSet L n to K is a number field, satisfies IsAbelianGalois over K, and satisfies IsRay for the ideal generated by n. weberSet, IsAbelianGalois and IsRay are unopened.

parts.name: discreteSeriesCoverExists
parts.gloss: For all p, q, every T of type GrpData p q and every rational-valued lam on Ix p q with IsParam lam, there exists R in DSRep T with HasParam R lam.

parts.name: siegelWeilUnitarySchrodinger
parts.gloss: For D of type D7, n and V with n < V.rank, V.rank ≤ 2 * n and n + wittIdx V < V.rank, and under unopened conditions on ψ, χ, θ, μ, ω, H, l, s, ν and Φ, three things hold. A descended theta function is integrable for every g, for every complex z with real part above n/2 the section sect ω H Φ z is LeftInv and satisfies Eis.CosetConv, and for every g the relation HolValueAt holds between the coset sum as a function of z, the point s0 V n and thetaInt ω ν Φ g.

parts.name: siegelEisensteinContinuation
parts.gloss: For D of type D7, V with 0 < V.rank, a with IsMaj V a and HasIwasawa, μ with IsHeckeChar and ResEta D μ b, a complex s₁ and φ in degPS V a μ s₁, the condition EisContinues V (flat V a φ s₁) holds, and for every s₀ there is a k with EisRegularAt V (flat V a φ s₁) s₀ k. These names are unopened.

parts.name: siegelEisensteinSimplePole
parts.gloss: Its type is UnusedSlot72, which the dossier shows to be an abbreviation for True. This field therefore asserts nothing, whatever its name says.

parts.name: schurOrthogonalitySquareIntegrable
parts.gloss: For a locally compact Hausdorff group G with a regular right-invariant Haar measure μ and a norm-preserving, strongly continuous homomorphism π into bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space H whose only closed invariant subspaces are zero and H, if one coefficient g ↦ ⟨w₀, π g v₀⟩ with nonzero v₀, w₀ is square-integrable then all coefficients are. Moreover there is a real d > 0 such that the integral of ⟨w, π g v⟩ times the conjugate of ⟨w', π g v'⟩ equals ⟨v', v⟩⟨w, w'⟩/d for all v, w, v', w'.

parts.name: litN
parts.gloss: A sub-bundle NonEndoscopicHypothesesAlt with five fields. They are loc (a bundle of 19 local statements), aut (a bundle of 16 global statements), coh (the bundle LitCoh of 12 statements), join (the five-fold conjunction JoinOut of unopened propositions) and fe (HeckeTateFunctionalEquation, which gives functions Λ and Λ' with IsCompletedL and Λ s = archEps n * finEps χ a s * Λ' (1 − s)).

parts.name: toHypothesesX
parts.gloss: A sub-bundle GeometricGaloisRepCompatibility with twelve fields. Ten repeat statements already listed above (weil, ds, ana, dsc, trc, dm, flath, sw, dbl, udbl), and the other two are HeckeLPartialContinuation (entire nonvanishing continuations on real part ≥ 1 for heckeL T χ and for (s − 1) times zetaOff T s) and HtCard, defined as the unopened PhtCmp.

parts.name: nLink
parts.gloss: A sub-bundle Hypotheses₂ with seven fields, namely FontaineBcris (seven unopened conditions on every C of type Core l), GlobalArtinReciprocity again, BlochKatoLocal (three unopened conditions), the three statements LocalTateDualityK, LocalEulerCharK and LocalFinitenessK, and BhattScholzeIntegral. The K-statements concern finite modules M over the integers mod l^r with a continuous action of GK l K and say that H0, H1, H2 are finite with Hn trivial for n ≥ 3, that card H1 = card H0 * card H2 * (card M)^(dimension of K over the l-adic numbers), and that certain cup-product maps are bijective.

parts.name: depthZeroSupport'
parts.gloss: The proposition DepthZeroSupport. For π in Irr k n with IsCuspSupport data σ, if π has a nonzero vector fixed by KOne k (Fin n) then every σ a has a nonzero vector fixed by KOne k (Fin (d a)).

parts.name: localFiniteness
parts.gloss: For every number field F with algebraic closure Ω, prime l, exponent r, finite discrete module M over the integers mod l^r, valuation subring A of Ω, representation rho of Dec A on M and prime v of F, the unopened condition LocalFinitenessAt A rho v holds.

parts.name: localTateDuality
parts.gloss: The same quantifiers as localFiniteness, with the unopened conclusion LocalTateDualityAt A rho v.

parts.name: localEulerChar
parts.gloss: The same quantifiers as localFiniteness, with the unopened conclusion LocalEulerCharAt A rho v.

glossary.suggests: The names suggest a list of published theorems taken as assumptions for an argument about unitary groups and theta lifts, covering results attributed by name to Clozel, Green, Chebotarev, Bhatt and Scholze, Bernstein and Zelevinsky, Harish-Chandra, Casselman and Wallach, Jacquet and Shalika, Flath, Dixmier and Malliavin, the Siegel-Weil formula, the doubling method, class field theory and local Galois cohomology. This is a suggestion from the names only, and the name siegelEisensteinSimplePole in particular is misleading because its content is True.
glossary.why: The structure and the outer logical shape of all 60 fields are visible, but most of the statements rest on predicates and objects whose bodies the dossier does not reach, and five fields are bare names with no body.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.RL.LinkedAt
glossary.what: a proposition-valued function of two arguments (a predicate on a parameter record and a test relation)
glossary.says: LinkedAt takes a parameter record p and a relation r on pairs (slot, linkage) and returns a proposition. A slot is a predicate on tuples (K, X, f, T, c), where K is a context, X a record of stages, f a frame, T twisting data and c a core record over them. Unfolding the one visible layer Lg1, the proposition says that there exists a slot R such that both of the following hold. First, the condition the code calls LargeBaseCondition holds for the base predicate KPx, the slot IsBuiltE p.s and R. Second, r holds of the pointwise conjunction of the slot IsGoodE p.s with R, paired with the linkage BundleLinkage p.

parts.name: hL (implicit argument)
parts.gloss: This is a proof of the proposition RecTExists, which says that for every number field E, algebraic closure Ω, valuation subring A of Ω, finite place w of E and proof h that A lies over w, there exists a map rc satisfying a condition that the code calls IsRecT. It enters only as the index of the type of p.

parts.name: p
parts.gloss: This is a record of the type Parameters hL, whose four fields are R of type RPosition, N of type NormChoiceExtension hL, S of type SExt and Γ of type GeoP. The body uses it only through p.s, an object of the type Slots obtained by a projection the dossier does not show, and through BundleLinkage p.

parts.name: r
parts.gloss: This is an arbitrary relation that takes a slot and a linkage for BundleCondition and returns a proposition. A linkage here is a predicate on a context K, a point β of type BPt K, a real number c and a bundle b of type BundleCondition β.D β.O c.

parts.name: Lg1 (the outer shape)
parts.gloss: Lg1 KP Q Q' r' is by definition the statement that there exists a slot R with LargeBaseCondition KP Q R and r' (sAnd Q' R). Here sAnd Q' R is the slot that holds at (K, X, f, T, c) exactly when both Q' and R hold there.

parts.name: KPx (first argument of Lg1)
parts.gloss: This is the predicate on a base B and a frame f that is the conjunction of two statements. The first says that there exists δ of type FieldDat B.toPre with a condition that the code calls B.KsExact δ f, and the second is PrePin B.toPre, which says that the map iX' sends each frame vector of the space X' to the frame vector of the space X at index R.m having the same index number.

parts.name: IsBuiltE p.s (second argument of Lg1, the slot Q)
parts.gloss: This is the slot positionOf (BuiltE p.s). It holds at (K, X, f, T, c) when there exist w of type ColW X.B f T, Z of type w.Lt and a core c' over the stages w.st Z such that there exists b of the type that the code calls Built p.s K w Z c' satisfying a condition that the code calls EntC b.ker, and such that the dependent triple made of X.C, the later stages of X and c equals the triple (w.C, Z, c').

parts.name: LargeBaseCondition KPx (IsBuiltE p.s) R (first conjunct)
parts.gloss: This applies an operator that the code calls EvLg to the predicate on (K, B, f, T) which says that if KPx B f holds then, for all stage data C, W, V, S, N, G over B and every core c over the resulting stages, IsBuiltE p.s at that tuple implies R at that tuple. The dossier does not show the body of EvLg.

parts.name: IsGoodE p.s (third argument of Lg1, the slot Q')
parts.gloss: This is the slot positionOf (GoodE p.s), built in the same way as IsBuiltE p.s. Its inner condition GoodE is the conjunction of BuiltE p.s with a condition that the code calls GoodO (w.D Z) c.O.nch c.O.xd.

parts.name: fun S => r S (BundleLinkage p) (fourth argument of Lg1, giving the second conjunct)
parts.gloss: This feeds r the slot S together with the fixed linkage BundleLinkage p, so the second conjunct reads r (sAnd (IsGoodE p.s) R) (BundleLinkage p). BundleLinkage p is the linkage that holds at (K, β, c, b) when there exist q of type WPt p.s K and a bundle b' of type BundleCondition (q.w.D q.Z) q.O c such that the record type BundleWitness q b' is nonempty and the dependent triple (β.D, β.O, b) equals (q.w.D q.Z, q.O, b').

parts.name: Q and Lk (variables in scope)
parts.gloss: The surrounding section declares a slot Q and a linkage Lk, but neither appears in the signature or the body of LinkedAt. They play no role in what the definition states.

unopened: p.s (the projection from Parameters to Slots)
glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names hint that EvLg means "eventually, for all sufficiently large scale contexts", so that the first conjunct would say that built positions eventually lie in R over good bases. On the same footing, LinkedAt would say that r holds at the good built positions cut down by such an R, together with the linkage of bundles that have a witness at a weighted point of p.
glossary.why: The logical shape through Lg1, sAnd, positionOf, linkOf and KPx is fully visible, but the operator EvLg, the projection p.s and the inner conditions Built, EntC, GoodO and the content of BundleWitness rest on names the dossier does not open.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.Bl.parametersOfDependence
glossary.what: a function that builds a record
glossary.says: It is a function that takes a proof hL of the proposition that the code calls RecTExists and a real number cDep, and returns a record of the type that the code calls Parameters hL. That record type has four fields named R, N, S and Γ. The function fills R with the fixed choice RX, fills N with extensionWithList hL cDep, fills S with SExt.none and fills Γ with geoCl anyGeometry. The real number cDep enters only through the field N, where it appears as the constant CF inside one existence condition called ListPin.

parts.name: hL
parts.gloss: This argument is a proof of the proposition RecTExists. The text shows that proposition to say that for every number field E, every algebraic closure Ω of E, every valuation subring A of Ω and every height one prime w of the ring of integers of E with a proof h of the condition that the code calls IsPlaceOver A w, there exists a map rc that satisfies the condition that the code calls IsRecT h rc.

parts.name: cDep
parts.gloss: This argument is a real number. It is passed unchanged to extensionWithList, where it becomes the middle entry of the triple ⟨1, cDep, b⟩ that indexes an object of the type that the code calls GridData.

parts.name: result type Parameters hL
parts.gloss: The result is a record with four fields, R of the type RPosition, N of the type NormChoiceExtension hL, S of the type SExt and Γ of the type GeoP. The first three types are families that assign a type to each long tuple of project data (K, B, f, T, w, Z, Wt, p0 and further entries), and GeoP is a family that assigns a true or false statement to each triple made of a D7, a Core of it and a DivX of it.

parts.name: parametersOfExtension
parts.gloss: This helper takes N, S and Γ and returns the record ⟨RX, N, S, Γ⟩. So the field R is always RX, which sends each tuple of data ending in an object t of the type RowsT to the record type that the code calls RXs t.

parts.name: field N, extensionWithList hL cDep
parts.gloss: For each tuple of data this is the product of two types. The first is extensionWithLaw applied to the same data, which is itself the product of defaultExtension (an object of the type that the code calls RealExpansionExtraData) with a proof of BkLaw (w.D Z), the implication from the condition called RationalMapValues to the condition called BuRational. The second is a proof of ListPin for the data and cDep, which says that there exists a GridData G with index ⟨1, cDep, K.s.b⟩ satisfying both the condition called FieldHas G (embLL0 D) and the condition called IsLamTieFull D.ntw (lamOf G).

parts.name: field S, SExt.none
parts.gloss: This is the constant family that sends every tuple of eleven arguments to PUnit, the type with exactly one element. It therefore carries no data.

parts.name: field Γ, geoCl anyGeometry
parts.gloss: The predicate anyGeometry is true on every triple. The predicate geoCl Γ is the inductively generated closure GeoCl Γ, which holds wherever Γ holds and is carried from (D, J, X) to (setDiv D N h, coreS N h J, divTr N h X) by a step rule. Since the base rule already applies to every triple, the text shows this closure of the always true predicate to hold on every triple too.

glossary.suggests: The names suggest that hL is an assumed existence of a local Langlands reciprocity map, and that the record collects the adjustable parameters of a large membership statement, with cDep a constant of dependence that fixes the size of a grid or list of characters. This is a suggestion from the names and module paths only.
glossary.why: The top definition and its four field values are fully visible down to two or three levels, but the types they range over and the conditions inside ListPin, BkLaw and RXs rest on many names whose bodies the dossier did not show.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.R1.SlotNormCondition
glossary.what: a proposition (a property of three arguments Q, Lk and N), defined by specialising a general existence statement that the code calls Row
glossary.says: Given a slot predicate Q, a link predicate Lk on bundles of the type BundleCondition, and a property N of family classes, the definition is the proposition Row Q Lk H, where H sends a family class 𝒜 and a selection to the statement N (D3 3 𝒜) and ignores the selection. Unfolded one step, it states that there exists a map E, from parameter records of type Par to predicates on bundles, such that RowE Q Lk E holds, and such that for every family class 𝒜 and every raw selection σ for 𝒜, if IsSel Q Lk E 𝒜 σ holds then N holds of the family class D3 3 𝒜. Here D3 3 𝒜 is the class 𝒜 strengthened by a fixed list of further conditions, with the real constant 3 placed in the slot C0, and with the bound Fm.CYL ≤ 9 among the added conditions. A family class is a predicate on parameter families Fm of type FamP eps, for every real eps.

parts.name: Q : V4.Slot
parts.gloss: The first argument is a predicate that takes a context K of type Ctx, a record X of type Stages, a frame f of type Fr X.B.toPre, a record T of type TwDat X.B and an object of the type V4.Core K X f T, and returns a proposition. The definition only passes it on to Row.

parts.name: Lk : LkT BundleCondition
parts.gloss: The second argument is a predicate that takes a context K, a point β of type BPt K, a real number c and a bundle of type BundleCondition β.D β.O c, and returns a proposition. BundleCondition D O c is a record with seven fields R, S, P, pin, DH, C and B, where DH is a pair of natural numbers p with D.s.Del = p.1 as a rational and O.L.etaSz = D.R.m times p.2 as a real.

parts.name: N : FamClass → Prop
parts.gloss: The third argument is a property of family classes. A family class is a predicate that assigns a proposition to every parameter family Fm of type FamP eps, for every real eps.

parts.name: Row Q Lk (…)
parts.gloss: The body applies Row with the bundle type taken to be BundleCondition. Row Q Lk H says that there exists E, a map from Par to predicates on bundles over all D, O and c, such that RowE Q Lk E holds and such that for all 𝒜 and all raw selections σ, IsSel Q Lk E 𝒜 σ implies H 𝒜 σ. A raw selection for 𝒜 gives, for each family Fm in 𝒜, each real x above Fm.x1 and each index i in Fm.Ix x, a bundle over Fm.D x i, the object that the code calls objAt Fm x hx i, and the constant Fm.Csz.

parts.name: RowE Q Lk E (inside Row)
parts.gloss: This is the condition that the code calls EvP applied to the predicate on pairs κ, K which says that for every point β of BPt K with β.Is Q, every real c and every bundle b over β.D, β.O, c, if Lk K β c b holds then E κ β.D β.O c b holds. The wrapper EvP and the condition β.Is Q have no visible body.

parts.name: IsSel Q Lk E 𝒜 σ (inside Row)
parts.gloss: This says that for every real eps and every family Fm with 𝒜 Fm there exists a parameter record κ of type Par, with seven fields eps, C, cD, ch, C5, c6 and Cb, such that three things hold. They are the condition that the code calls Link κ Fm, the condition that the code calls DQ.cls7 with the trivially true predicate at Fm, and, for every x above Fm.x1 and every index i, both the condition that the code calls Built Q Lk κ at the selected bundle σ Fm hc x hx i and E κ at that same bundle.

parts.name: fun 𝒜 _ => N (D3 3 𝒜)
parts.gloss: This is the conclusion H handed to Row. It ignores the selection and asserts N of the class D3 3 𝒜, which is Des (WithChN 𝒜) 3. WithChN 𝒜 holds of Fm when 𝒜 Fm, DGamDvdF Fm, TameDistinctF Fm, BoxesF Fm, QDRowsF Fm and Fm.CYL ≤ 9 all hold. Des of that class with constant 3 adds DGamSmooth Fm, TwGood Fm, the existence of a real CH with ChosenE Fm 3 CH, TuSize Fm and DGamSize Fm.

unopened: the field types of BundleCondition (RecTAlt, STiesRAlt, RowSideFamily, RowSideDeterminedAlt, SquareIntegrableColumns, RealTBAlt) below their field lists
glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names hint that this is a "norm" condition attached to a "slot" of a construction, which would say that eventually in the parameters (EvP), every bundle built at a point in slot Q and linked by Lk satisfies some property E, and any family class whose members can all be served by such bundles has its strengthened "design" class D3 3 𝒜 satisfying N. The module names mention theta correspondence and abelian varieties, but the text shown does not confirm what any of that means here.
glossary.why: The logical shape of the definition, Row, IsSel, RowE, D3, Des and WithChN are all visible with their constants 3 and 9, but the key conditions EvP, β.Is, Link, DQ.cls7 and Built, and most of the underlying data types, have no visible bodies.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.NLink.BoundAtTwoThreeFamilyFonAlt
glossary.what: a proposition about a family record Fm of the type that the code calls FamP eps, where eps is a real number
glossary.says: It is a proposition that depends on a real number eps and on a record Fm of the type FamP eps. It states that there exist real numbers C and x0 such that the following holds for every real x with x ≥ x0, every proof hx that Fm.x1 < x, every index i in Fm.Ix x, every HW, every F, every piece of comparison data built over F, every record X of type HubData for the datum Fm.D x i, and every real number C₂. If the condition SetupAlt holds for Fm.L x i, the component nch of Fm.ex x hx i, HW, X and C₂, then the condition BoundAtTwoThree holds for Fm.L x i, the component ρ of X, and the constant C. The constants C and x0 are chosen once, before x, i and all the other data, so the same C serves the whole family. The objects F and the comparison data are quantified over, yet they appear neither in the hypothesis SetupAlt nor in the conclusion.

parts.name: eps
parts.gloss: An implicit real number that only serves as the parameter of the type FamP eps of the family.

parts.name: Fm
parts.gloss: A record of the structure FamP eps, which extends an unshown structure FamCore eps. The definition uses its components x1, Ix, D and L, which come from the unshown FamCore, and its field ex, which for each x with x1 < x and each i in Ix x gives a record of the type called Extra.

parts.name: ∃ C x0 : ℝ
parts.gloss: Two real numbers are asserted to exist, placed outside all the other quantifiers. C is the constant handed to the conclusion and x0 is a threshold for x.

parts.name: ∀ x ≥ x0
parts.gloss: The statement is required for every real number x that is at least x0.

parts.name: hx : Fm.x1 < x
parts.gloss: A proof that x exceeds the number Fm.x1 of the family. It is needed because the field ex of Fm is only defined for such x.

parts.name: i : Fm.Ix x
parts.gloss: An index taken from the index type Fm.Ix x that the family attaches to x. It selects the datum Fm.D x i, which the header's variable declaration suggests is of type D7, and the object Fm.L x i.

parts.name: HW : HWOf (Fm.D x i).loc
parts.gloss: By the shown body of HWOf this is a choice, for every prime number l, of a record of the structure LocHW at l over the l-th component of (Fm.D x i).loc. LocHW has fields W, W_s and W_proj, whose types rest on the unshown names LocWach, Good and FinExt.

parts.name: F : FonOf (Fm.D x i).loc (Fm.D x i).locA HW
parts.gloss: By the shown body of FonOf this is a choice, for every prime l, of a record of the structure LocFon at l. That record has one field E, which for each K, s, LL and proof of Good K s LL gives an object of the type that the code calls EtSit.

parts.name: unnamed argument of type CmpOf (Fm.D x i).loc (Fm.D x i).locA HW F
parts.gloss: By the shown body of CmpOf this is a choice, for every prime l, of a record of the structure LocCmpT at l built over F. That record has one field C, which gives objects of the type that the code calls CmpSit. The argument has no name and is not used afterwards.

parts.name: X : KillingConditions.HubData (Fm.D x i)
parts.gloss: A record of the structure HubData for the datum Fm.D x i, with fields r, ρ, len0, errorBoundHub, dc, lenRow, e', cB, eS, c0, band, exc, eta and I. The whole record goes into the hypothesis and only its field ρ, of the type called RhoFam, goes into the conclusion.

parts.name: C₂ : ℝ
parts.gloss: A real number, universally quantified, which appears only in the hypothesis SetupAlt, where it enters through the expression rowC C₂.

parts.name: hypothesis SetupAlt (Fm.L x i) (Fm.ex x hx i).nch HW X C₂
parts.gloss: A proposition given as a record of eight conditions named facts, canon, par, par67, big, split, kill and sha. Two of them are readable, namely big, which says 8 ≤ L.sc.L, and split, which says 60 ≤ D.host.splitBound, where splitBound is a natural number field of the host record. The other six are conditions that the code calls NormChoiceFacts, HubX.Canon, AdmPar, ParametersPolynomiallyBounded, KillAt (applied to X.ρ) and ShaFinOdd.

parts.name: conclusion BoundAtTwoThree (Fm.L x i) X.ρ C
parts.gloss: By its shown body, with D standing for Fm.D x i and L for Fm.L x i, this says the following. For every i' for which the condition called TwLoc D i' holds, and for which either D.nd.l i' = 2 or both D.nd.l i' = 3 and D.nd.l i' is not in D.host.small, every π in the set D.nd.Zgood i' satisfies the condition that the code calls Bd, applied to ρ, i', π and the quantity midF L C.

unopened: FamCore (source of Fm.x1, Fm.Ix, Fm.D, Fm.L)
glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names point to a uniform bound, with one constant C for a whole family of arithmetic data indexed by a growing real parameter x, on some quantity attached to local places of residue characteristic 2 and 3. The words Fon and Alt suggest a variant of an earlier family statement that additionally assumes local p-adic Hodge theoretic data (Wach module style data HW, data F perhaps named after Fontaine, and a comparison) under an alternative set of setup hypotheses.
glossary.why: The quantifier structure, the two numerical conditions 8 ≤ L.sc.L and 60 ≤ D.host.splitBound, and the case split at 2 and 3 are fully visible, but the family core FamCore, the bound Bd with midF, and six of the eight setup conditions have no body in the dossier.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.Bl.KPx
glossary.what: a predicate (a proposition-valued function) on pairs made of a record B of type Base and a record f of type Fr B.toPre
glossary.says: KPx is an element of the type BaseP, which the dossier shows to be the type of functions that take a record B of type Base and a record f of type Fr B.toPre and return a proposition. For given B and f, KPx B f is the conjunction of two statements. The first statement says that there exists a record δ of type FieldDat B.toPre such that a condition that the code calls B.KsExact holds of δ and f. The second statement is PrePin B.toPre, which says that the linear map iX' of the underlying Pre record sends each basis vector of the space X' to the basis vector with the same index in the space X at index R.m. The second statement does not depend on f.

parts.name: B
parts.gloss: B is a record of type Base, which extends the record type Pre. On top of the Pre data it adds a number field LL that is Galois over ℚ with a star operation and an embedding embLL into ℂ, a ring map embE from the host field E into LL, two intermediate fields LL0 and Ks with Ks inside LL0, and conditions asking for certain roots of unity in Ks, LL0 and LL and for ideals of E to become principal in Ks.

parts.name: f
parts.gloss: f is a record of type Fr B.toPre, which unfolds to Chr.HFrame B.host with exponent function sending j and g to the entry e j of B.hc g. Such a record holds an object P of type PiBar (a choice of a prime of the field K above each of the two primes g 0 and g 1), an object W of type Omg (an injective character of the units of the integers modulo g k for each k), characters mu0 j, eta, chiPsi, del and del' of type HChar of the host field E, and proofs of the conditions IsMu0, IsEtaT, IsChiPsi, and IsDelta at the primes pde and pde'.

parts.name: first conjunct, ∃ δ : Fld.FieldDat B.toPre, B.KsExact δ f
parts.gloss: This says that some record δ of type FieldDat for the Pre part of B exists for which the condition that the code calls B.KsExact holds of δ and f. The dossier shows no body for KsExact, so what the condition demands is not visible.

parts.name: δ
parts.gloss: δ is a record of type FieldDat P with P equal to B.toPre. It holds a subfield ray of ℂ with a proof of IsRayFieldIn for the embedding φ₀ and the ideal of the integers of E generated by the natural number g 0 * g 1 * pde * pde', a subfield jField of ℂ, a Weierstrass curve over jField with a proof of IsGoodCMCurve for the number d, and a ClassBasis of E, which is a finite family of invertible fractional ideals c i and units γ i whose classes generate the class group independently and satisfy c i raised to the order of its class equals the principal ideal of γ i.

parts.name: second conjunct, PrePin B.toPre
parts.gloss: With the star structure that the code calls host.cmStar in force, this says that for every index a below the rank of the space sp.X' and every index b below the rank of the space sp.X R.m, if a and b are equal as natural numbers then the linear map sp.iX' sends the a-th vector of the stored basis (frame) of X' to the b-th vector of the stored basis of X R.m. The symbol ∀ means for all, and Fin n is the set of natural numbers below n.

unopened: the fields of Host, Spaces, HostDer and HostRaw that lie past the cuts
the HChar conditions IsUnitary, UnrAt, TameAt, TrivOn, HasInf, HasInfQ, ResEta, OrderDvd, loc and locK
glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the name KsExact hints that the field Ks of B is required to be exactly some field built from the data δ, such as a compositum involving the ray field and the field of the CM curve, in a way tied to the characters in f. The name PrePin hints at pinning the frame of X' to the initial segment of the frame of the top space X.
glossary.why: The overall shape, the types of B, f and δ, and the whole second conjunct are visible, but the central condition KsExact in the first conjunct has no body in the dossier.

glossary.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.BundleCondition
glossary.what: a record type (a structure with seven fields, living in the universe Type 1) that depends on three parameters
glossary.says: For a base datum D of type D7, an object O of type Obj D and a real number c, BundleCondition D O c is the type of records that bundle seven components built over the component O.ex of O. Five components are data, namely a record R, a record S that depends on R, a record P, a record C that depends on R.T and P, and a record B that depends on R, P, C, S and a scale function. One component, pin, is a proof of a proposition about R.T and P. One component, DH, is a pair of natural numbers together with a proof of two equations, the first saying that D.s.Del equals the first number read as a rational, and the second saying that O.L.etaSz equals the real number D.R.m times the second number. The real number c enters only through B, where the scale function zsc P DH.1.1 DH.1.2 c is formed from P, the two natural numbers of DH and c.

parts.name: D
parts.gloss: This argument is a record of the type that the code calls D7, a large structure whose first fields are a rank record R, a host record, spaces, a positive volume function and a rows record called what₂. The dossier shows only the first 3,000 of the 9,862 characters of D7.

parts.name: O
parts.gloss: This argument is a record of type Obj D, which the dossier shows to have eight fields L, gatT, Gx, Gy, K, X, cX and ex. The last field ex has the type Extra D L gatT Gx Gy K X cX, and it is O.ex that most of the fields below are built over.

parts.name: c
parts.gloss: This argument is a real number. It is used only in the last field, where it is passed to the function zsc.

parts.name: R
parts.gloss: This field is a record of type RecTAlt O.ex. The dossier shows that such a record has five fields, namely T of the type called TiedDataSKAlt O.ex, pin of the type called RowPinMinAlt T, joints of the type called JointsSAlt, host of the type called HostDatumSelfDual, and weq of the type called WeilCompatibleEquivariance, and none of these five types is opened.

parts.name: S
parts.gloss: This field is a record of type STiesRAlt R. The dossier shows that it extends a record called STies D and adds, for every word u, a transport tr u with conditions called ColDictInto, ColDictBij and LevelMatch, an equation colPin that identifies a column dictionary value with D.s_Cu u x, an equation inst, an object G of the type called GoodOp, a condition rowTie and a condition called LocTied D.

parts.name: P
parts.gloss: This field is a record of type RowSideFamily O.ex. The dossier shows that it holds a finite group Gp, three further types Pl0, I0 and T, an object A3 of the type called FamIn3, two subgroups P0 and Ps of Gp with homomorphisms ψ0 and ψs into the units of the field D.what₂.LL, an object Zs of the type called DefSub, and further objects S0, S1, Dc, Sp, C, NuC, I, JA, JM and tied whose types are not opened.

parts.name: pin
parts.gloss: This field is a proof of the proposition RowSideDeterminedAlt R.T P. The dossier shows that proposition to be a conjunction of six named conditions, lowerMap, lowerMapTw, buDef, ambS, faces and gamDvd. The condition faces says that there exist families Dcf and Spf indexed by all Zs whose values at P.Zs are P.Dc and P.Sp, and gamDvd says that the cardinalities of certain finite sets Gam c divide the natural number (D.mem D.u₀).C.DGam.

parts.name: DH
parts.gloss: This field is a pair p of natural numbers together with a proof that D.s.Del equals p.1 read as a rational number and that O.L.etaSz equals the real number D.R.m times p.2 read as a real number. Here D.R.m is the field m of the rank record, which the dossier shows to be an even natural number that is at least 2, while D.s and O.L.etaSz are not opened.

parts.name: C
parts.gloss: This field is a record of type SquareIntegrableColumns R.T P. The dossier shows that it holds an object X of the type called Fields, a family e of ring homomorphisms into D.what₂.LL, an object c of the type called ColRec3, a family Sp, conditions called ColTie3 and ColumnRecordCompatible, an infinite place v0 of D.what₂.LL, a finite set TU, and equations that identify P.A3, P.Gp, P.Pl0, P.I0 and P.T with objects built from c and X.

parts.name: B
parts.gloss: This field is a record of type RealTBAlt R P C.c.face C.Sp (zsc P DH.1.1 DH.1.2 c) S, so it takes the two families from C, the record S and a scale function. The dossier shows that zsc sends each Zs to the object z given by ZscOfNum3 applied to P.A3, P.P0, P.ψ0, ofRecord D O.L Del h0, an identity bijection, O.L.Nc and Zs, and then replaces the component l6m j by z.l6m j minus c times z.l6u and sets the component l6u to 0. The record RealTBAlt itself has fields T, alg, Q, κ, v₀, fw, bar, O, pins, rhoGeo, equivAll, cTie and phase, whose types (CoreJ, IndefiniteRealisation, FWTie, BarTie, OMDat, OMPins, RhoGeo, EquivAll, CTie, PhaseTie) are not opened.

glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names point to a package of compatibility data for a theta correspondence construction, with row-side and column-side families, spectral ties, square-integrable columns and a real realisation of an indefinite form, where c shifts a scale parameter. The field D.s is probably a record of the visible type SData, whose field Del is a positive rational, so DH would say that this rational is a natural number and that a size parameter etaSz is m times a natural number, but the dossier does not show the field D.s itself.
glossary.why: The dossier shows the full text of the structure, the field lists of all seven field types and the body of zsc, but almost every type inside those field lists, and the cut part of D7 containing D.s, remains unopened.

glossary.name: Formalism.IndefR.Cx.CxData.MIstar2
glossary.what: a proposition (a true-or-false statement) that depends on a data record X, a map fc and two further maps eV and sEE
glossary.says: MIstar2 is a proposition attached to a record X of the type CxData A, where A is a record of type DefAmb Bs over a number field K with a star operation. Besides X it takes a function fc from DefSub A to DefFace Bs, a family of K-linear maps eV and a conjugate-linear map sEE. It states that there exists an object d of the type that the code calls X.MIDat fc such that three conditions hold together, namely the condition that the code calls X.MIUnit2 d, the condition that the code calls X.MIid eV sEE d, and the condition that the code calls X.AuNZ d. The dossier shows no body for any of these four names, so the text only shows the shape of the statement, which is one existential quantifier over d followed by a conjunction of three conditions. No numbers or constants appear in it.

parts.name: X
parts.gloss: X is a record of type CxData A. The dossier shows that such a record holds, among other fields, finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces FC t, EE, FLC j t and W j, maps jR and jL into them from the K-modules A.FR t and A.FL j t that are semilinear along the embedding of the place Bs.v0, complex linear maps Θ and θ', several families of subspaces, and real-valued and index-valued parameters.

parts.name: fc
parts.gloss: fc is a function that sends each record of type DefSub A (a choice of K-submodules Z t of A.FR t and Zl j t of A.FL j t) to a record of type DefFace Bs. A DefFace holds two records Df0 and Df1 of type DefSide Bs, a record Dc of type DefCols Df1, a record Sp of type SPer Dc and a record Z of type IndefScale Bs.

parts.name: eV
parts.gloss: eV gives, for every index t in the type Bs.Tup, a K-linear map from the space of n-tuples of elements of K into the K-module A.FR t. Here n is the natural number (fc X.zs).Df1.nV t, which is the field nV of the side Df1 of the face that fc assigns to X.zs, and X.zs is an object that the dossier does not define.

parts.name: sEE
parts.gloss: sEE is a conjugate-linear map over the complex numbers (additive, and sending a scalar multiple c times x to the complex conjugate of c times the image of x) from the space X.EE to the space (fc X.zs).Sp.HH. The dossier shows X.EE to be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and HH to be a type with a normed group structure and a complex inner product, taken from the field Sp of the face fc X.zs.

parts.name: ∃ d : X.MIDat fc
parts.gloss: The statement begins by asserting that there exists some d, an object of the type that the code calls X.MIDat fc. The dossier does not show what such an object consists of.

parts.name: X.MIUnit2 d
parts.gloss: The first conjunct is a condition on d that the code calls X.MIUnit2. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: X.MIid eV sEE d
parts.gloss: The second conjunct is a condition that the code calls X.MIid, and it is the only one of the three that involves the maps eV and sEE together with d. Its body is not shown.

parts.name: X.AuNZ d
parts.gloss: The third conjunct is a condition on d that the code calls X.AuNZ. Its body is not shown.

glossary.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names and the module title (isometric periods of unit hypotheses) hint that MIDat is a package of data for a map or period identity, that MIUnit2 is a unit-type hypothesis on it, that MIid is an identity relating that data to eV and sEE, and that AuNZ is a non-vanishing condition. The typing of fc suggests that X.zs is a record of type DefSub A attached to X, although it is not among the fields of CxData shown.
glossary.why: The logical shape and the types of the arguments are fully visible, but the type of the witness d, all three conditions on it and the object X.zs have no body in the dossier, so the mathematical content of the statement cannot be seen.

d7.says: An object of D7 is one large bundle of number-theoretic data together with the equations that tie the pieces to each other. It starts from integer parameters (a Ranks record R), a CM number field setting (a Host record with fields E and F, primes q, d, g 0, g 1, pde, pde' and a finite set of level primes), and families of Hermitian spaces over E. It then adds a second number field LL with its places and a finite set of words. There is one rational parameter record for each word and each element of a set Tau of size f, and each word also has a member made of column data, data at a prime T and a period map. On top of this it adds a determinant group Dt with characters that fix the values rhoDet and rhoDet', p-adic period rings for every prime l, a large package of Galois-representation and automorphic data (the N-stage records), Hermitian lattice forms, Haar measures on the groups U(P,Q), theta-jet data at chosen primes, and local data at good primes. Many of the fields are conditions that make these independently given pieces agree, and the group sections below say which fields hold data and which hold conditions.
d7.suggests: As a suggestion only, the names hint that D7 is the full set of hypotheses for one step of a large argument, the step named in its module RhoDetPrimeEqMuTildeMulChiPow, which writes the column values rhoDet and rhoDet' as values of characters on a determinant group. The names Host, cmType, Psi and condN suggest a CM field with a CM type and a conductor, and the period-ring names (Ainf, Bcris, BdR, LocTied) suggest Fontaine's p-adic Hodge theory. The N-stage names (heckePol, frobEig, IsCrysW, csd and the Speh-style sums) suggest Galois representations attached to conjugate self-dual automorphic representations of unitary groups. The names ThetaJet, HCParam and CDHaar, together with the Hermitian lattices, suggest theta lifts and harmonic-analysis estimates, but the file gives no bodies for many of these names, so these readings remain guesses.

groups.title: Ranks, host field, spaces and volumes
groups.gloss: R is a Ranks record of natural numbers k, m, t (k and m even, t odd, 2 ≤ m, m + 3 ≤ k, k + m − 1 + 5 ≤ t, 3m < t, m ≤ 2·ord ≤ k and m² ≤ k + m(t + 1)). host is a Host record over R that supplies a CM number field E together with two number fields that the code calls F and K, primes q and d, a number QS, two distinct level primes g 0 and g 1, two further level primes pde and pde' that leave remainder 1 on division by 15, and an ideal ccK. The field sp is a Spaces record over E, meaning a CM extension E over a totally real F of degree 2, a prime T, and Hermitian spaces X j, X', Y j, W j and V j over E with prescribed ranks, embeddings and signatures. The function vol gives each Hermitian space a real number, and vol_pos requires that number to be strictly positive.

groups.title: Row data and the base parameters
groups.gloss: what₂ is a Rows.Data record over R. It holds a field LL with an embedding embLL into the complex numbers and a system of places, a finite set Tau with exactly f elements, finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces such as EE (with Drows = (1 − delp)·Dall and delp ≤ 1), a type Word, and spaces Mu u, Amb μ and Mt μ j with lattices and self-adjoint idempotent operators. eTau is a bijection between Tau and a set the code calls R.Psi. hc assigns to each τ in Tau an HCParam record, which is a list u of k half-integers, a list v of k − 1 integers and lists b and e of m integers that interlace (v i < u i and u (i+1) < v i, and −b 0 < u (k−1)), with e j − b j ≥ (t + 3)/2 and b (j+1) − e j ≥ (t + 3)/2.

groups.title: Words and their parameters and members
groups.gloss: The set of words is finite, and u₀ is a chosen base word. The function hcW gives one HCParam record for each word u and each τ, and it agrees with hc at the base word. For every word the entries v, b and e are the same as those of hc, and so are the first entry u 0 and the last entry u (k−1) when k > 0, so only the inner entries of u may change from word to word. For each word, mem u is a Member made of three parts, a column chain C (finite class sets cls i with finite stabilizer groups whose orders divide a positive number DGam, values rhoDet and rhoDet' of absolute value 1 for i < m, and integers sSharp and sDiv given by the functions sExp' and sExp at e i and i + 1, which this reading takes to be e i − N(i+1)/2 and e i − N(i)/2), a ColumnsAtT record A (a prime T, a set vT of f elements, finite fields Fv of size T, nontrivial additive characters, a positive Dstar and a number GamP > 1) and a period map P.

groups.title: The field LL
groups.gloss: LL is a number field, that is a finite extension of the rational numbers, and it carries an involution called star. LL is totally complex and is a Galois extension of the rationals. The embedding embLL into the complex numbers sends star x to the complex conjugate of embLL x.

groups.title: Hermitian lattice data over LL
groups.gloss: div is a DivData record over LL indexed by the words. It consists of a Hermitian lattice RR, one lattice Nu u per word, linear maps Bk u from Nu u into the dual of RR, real numbers h u, HH, etaF and delP, and a natural number Dall, with delP ≤ 1 and HH at least the rank-weighted average of the differences between mu (Nu u) and h u plus RR.muMax. div_good requires that every matrix X v attached to RR and to each Nu u at each infinite place v has a determinant that is a unit, so that it is invertible.

groups.title: Embedding the host field into LL
groups.gloss: embE is a ring homomorphism from E to LL whose composite with embLL is the chosen complex embedding host.φ₀ of E. conjF is an F-linear field map of E equal to the map the code calls host.conj, and embE turns host.conj into star. LL0 is a subfield of LL that contains the image of E. Every element of the ring what₂.O maps to an algebraic integer of LL, and the image of every algebraic integer of E is hit by some element of what₂.O.

groups.title: Places of LL
groups.gloss: plEq is a bijection between the abstract places of what₂ and the nonzero prime ideals of the ring of integers of LL. For nonzero x, the valuation at a place w equals the w-adic order of x, defined as minus the logarithm of the multiplicative valuation (vAdd). The stored ramification index at w equals the ramification index of the prime over the integers (eWL), and the valuation of x at the conjugate place equals the valuation at w of star x.

groups.title: The prime T of each word
groups.gloss: For each word u, the prime T(u) of its member lies in the level primes of the host, and it equals π times host.conj π for an algebraic integer π of E lying in K with π − 1 divisible by QS·q·d·(g 0·g 1)². The prime of the spaces sp is T(u₀), and for each word there is a nonzero c in E with c·conj(c)·T(u) = T(u₀). Each T(u) lies between Tstar and (1 + 1/(f·k))·Tstar, where Tstar is a quantity the code calls (mem u).A.Tstar. GamP is the same for every word, T(u) differs from pde and from pde', and Dstar equals what₂.Dstar.

groups.title: Lattices for the column classes
groups.gloss: For each word u, each level i and each class c in cls i, clsLat gives a submodule over the ring of integers of E inside the space (sp.X i).V. clsLat_lat requires each of these to be a full lattice in that E-vector space, in the sense of Submodule.IsFullLattice.

groups.title: Identifications with period data
groups.gloss: eMu u is a complex-linear isomorphism from what₂.Mu u to a space the code calls Mram, and eMt u is a complex-linear isomorphism from the space Mt of the period map to Amb at the base tuple mu0. At the base tuple the pairing perCol equals a map the code calls PtilCol, read through these isomorphisms, and the pairing Bu is linear in each argument. For each tuple μ there is a twisted column chain chTw u μ that equals the member's chain at mu0, with linear isomorphisms e0Tw and eMtTw and a period map PTw. For μ different from mu0, perCol is again PtilCol of PTw, read through these identifications.

groups.title: Bases matching LL lattices with complex spaces
groups.gloss: jEE is an additive map from the LL-space of RR into EE that is semilinear with respect to embLL, meaning jEE(a x) = embLL(a)·jEE(x). It sends the basis of RR to a basis of the complex space EE, and in the same way jN u sends the basis of Nu u to a basis of Mu u. The numbers Dall and delP of div agree with Dall and delp of what₂.

groups.title: Determinant group and its characters
groups.gloss: Dt is a commutative group, detCls sends each class to Dt, muTil n and chiD are homomorphisms from Dt to the nonzero complex numbers, and chiD is trivial on a subgroup UO. e1Dt maps the unitary elements z of E (those with star z · z = 1) to Dt, and chiD(e1Dt z) is the product over τ in Tau of the inverse of host.emb(eTau τ)(z). For self-dual lattices in E^N (finitely generated, spanning, and equal to their dual for the form sum of star(x i)·y i), relDet gives an element of Dt/UO that is 1 on equal lattices, multiplies along chains L, L', L'' and equals the class of e1Dt(det γ) when L' is the image of L under a unitary matrix γ. Finally rhoDet i c equals muTil(i+1) of detCls to the power −1 times chiD of detCls to the power −⌊N(i+1)/2⌋, and rhoDet' i c equals muTil(i+1) of detCls times chiD of detCls to the power ⌊N(i)/2⌋.

groups.title: Positive weights on Tau
groups.gloss: dsig gives a real number for each element of Tau. dsig_pos requires every one of these numbers to be strictly positive.

groups.title: Cusp-span data
groups.gloss: s is an SData record built from R, F, E, conjF, the words, Tau and hcW. It holds a positive rational Del with consecutive v entries differing by exactly 4·Del, an injective letter map from words to sequences of k − 2 booleans with u(l+1) = v l − 1/2 − Del when the letter is true and v l − 1/2 otherwise, a finite-dimensional complex inner product space HH with spaces Cu u and maps into it, positive volumes, terms and pairs, and local field data atP at each prime of F with a degree 2 extension. The split datum at p is present exactly when the residue characteristic of p is g 0 or g 1, HH has complex dimension what₂.Dall, Cu u is linearly isomorphic to the member's space Mu0, and the places PlF correspond bijectively to the nonzero primes of the ring of integers of F.

groups.title: Local p-adic period theory
groups.gloss: loc gives a LocPrime record for every prime l. That is a pair of rings B and BdR with Galois actions, a Frobenius map φB, an element tB, a character χQ, period data for every finite extension of the l-adic numbers, compatible l-power roots of unity ζQ, and valuations normalised by v(l) = 1. For each l, locA adds actions on the completed algebraic closure and on its tilt, an element ε built from roots of unity, and an injective map from A_inf into B that respects the Galois action, Frobenius and the filtration. locT identifies B and BdR with the rings Bcris and BdR that the project builds from Witt vectors of the tilt, compatibly with the l-adic integers, the Galois actions, Frobenius, the filtrations, an element t that is a logarithm of the Teichmüller lift of ε, and A_inf.

groups.title: Galois and automorphic stage data
groups.gloss: nd is an NData record. It holds an algebraic closure Om of E and a set Loc of local indices i, each with a prime l i, a level j i with 1 ≤ j i ≤ m, and a complete discrete valuation ring O i finite over the l-adic integers. It also holds a local Hecke algebra acting faithfully on a free module, characters chi i c equal to chi i 1 times the cyclotomic character to the power −(c − 1) for 1 ≤ c ≤ t, sets S i and Q i of split places, sets PlG k of size f with monic labels of degree r, and the identity restRowsFiniteGroupCard = ∏ over k of |GL_r(ℤ/g k)|^f. ntw (NTw) gives twisting data with characters delta whose inertia image has exactly 15 elements at auxiliary places of norm ≡ 1 mod 15, naut (NAut) gives abstract local parameters with dimension, sums, twists and Frobenius eigenvalues together with automorphic objects CG a, nbc (NBC), nexp (NExp) and nth (NTh) give base-change, expansion and theta data, and ntypes (NTypes) gives an abelian extension Mray of K unramified outside primes dividing QS·q·d, with g k ≡ 1 mod QS·q·d and multisets bc with sum of a·d equal to r. The two remaining fields require a condition that the code calls ntypes.IdempotentMatchesAction and require embLL(eLL0 g) to equal the coefficient at g of an element the code calls ntypes.e0.

groups.title: Local bridges at primes above l
groups.gloss: For each local index i and each prime w of E above l i, nbr gives a LocBridge. That is a finite extension Kw of the l-adic numbers in which E is dense, an embedding j of Om into the algebraic closure of the l-adic numbers, a continuous isomorphism between the decomposition group at w and the Galois group of Kw, and a larger extension LL containing all conjugates of Kw whose ring of integers is isomorphic to O i. nbr_ind requires x to lie in the valuation ring at w exactly when |j x| ≤ 1, and self_good requires every root of unity whose order divides lcm(l, host.condN) to lie in that LL. ntwbr and ntwbr_ind give the same kind of bridge, with the same condition, for the twist indices and the rings O0.

groups.title: Tie conditions between stages
groups.gloss: The field loc_tie requires that iotaOQ agrees with the bridge map toLL, and that the NAut predicates the code calls IsCrysW, IsdRW and IsPotCrysW and the jump multisets jumpsW agree, through the local bridges and loc, with the bridge notions the code calls IsCrysW, IsdRW, IsPotCrysW, IsJumpW and multW and with their versions IsCrysE, IsdRE, IsPotCrysE, IsJumpE and multE over larger finite extensions. bc_tie requires bc σ to equal the multiset of pairs (a, d) for any matching parameter list whose automorphic pieces satisfy a condition the code calls csd and an integrality condition, and rbar_tie requires rbar to be semisimple with characteristic polynomials that reduce correctly. mtpar_tie requires MtPar to be the span of the matching typeV spaces, and Z i and Zgood i equal the explicitly defined sets ZN and ZgoodN (points whose parameter list contains the part (1, muC i twisted by etaTinv, t)). For 1 ≤ j ≤ m, etaJ_tie requires etaJ j w to equal the sum of a quantity the code calls nd.etaLoc over the local indices with level j and place w.

groups.title: Hermitian forms of members and isometries
groups.gloss: fm u is a MemberForms record for member u. It holds vector spaces of dimension N i over the fields Fv, dominant integer weights lam given by an explicit formula from hc, Hermitian lattices lat i over LL embedded in the class-function spaces with matching norms, and nonnegative reals beOn and thFree. The inner product on Mu u equals a form the code calls ipC 0, read through eMu, and the same holds for Cu u through s_Cu. nuIn u is an injective LL-linear map from the lattice space of Nu u into the space of lat 0, with image a subspace the code calls ramSub, compatible with jN and eMu, and preserving the coordinate norm normAt at every infinite place, while jEE preserves norms at the infinite place of embLL and sEE is a conjugate-linear isometric embedding of EE into s.HH.

groups.title: Haar measures on unitary groups
groups.gloss: cd is a CDHaar record giving a Haar measure on each group U(P,Q) of complex matrices preserving the form with matrix diag(1 for P entries, −1 for Q entries). The measure on U(N,0) is a probability measure. For each P and Q there is one constant c, neither 0 nor infinite, that is the limiting density near the identity of both cd P Q and cd (P+Q) 0 against a Lebesgue-normalised measure on the Lie algebra.

groups.title: Theta-jet sites
groups.gloss: jet is a ThetaJet record with sites of two kinds. A site of the first kind carries a prime l ≥ 5, an even d ≥ 2, ranks N0 = N(jOf − 1) and N1 = N(jOf) with 1 ≤ jOf ≤ m, and a power series in variables indexed by ℤ/d × {0..N0−1} × {0..N1−1}, and a site of the second kind has d replaced by 1, the host class of l equal to the inert class, and a condition HNeZero that fails. For each site of the first kind the fields choose a word, a class at level jOf − 1 and a class at level jOf of that word's chain, a place of LL whose residue characteristic is the site's prime l, and a map from ℤ/d into Tau. Sites of the second kind get the same choices, with one element of Tau instead of a map.

groups.title: Extra global data and local data at good primes
groups.gloss: gx is a GlobalExtra record giving strictly positive reals Om τ s and thOne s for each τ and each complex embedding s of LL. For each word u and place w whose residue characteristic p satisfies GIdx (p prime, p ≥ 5, inert class, HNeZero, p not a level prime and p not dividing T(u)), gat gives a GAtP record at p, which is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field, place data satisfying HidaSetting, and a number e. The field gat_d requires a quantity named d to equal the complex dimension of the member's space Mu0. The file gives no body for this d, and d is a different number from the field e of GAtP.

groups.title: Signature of the spaces Y j
groups.gloss: For every j ≤ m and every complex embedding τ of E, the signature of the Hermitian space sp.Y j at τ is the pair sigYD R j. That pair is (rankY j − ⌊(m − j)/2⌋, ⌊(m − j)/2⌋), where rankY is a rank the code calls R.rankY.

numbers: In D7, vol_pos requires vol W > 0 for every Hermitian space W, and dsig_pos requires dsig ρ > 0.
In D7, T_norm requires π − 1 to be divisible by QS·q·d·(g 0·g 1)².
In D7, T_win requires Tstar ≤ T(u) ≤ (1 + 1/(f·k))·Tstar for every word u.
In D7, hcW_first and hcW_last fix the entries of u at index 0 and at index k − 1 when 0 < k.
In D7, rhoDet_eq_inv_muTilde_chiD_pow uses the exponent −⌊N(i+1)/2⌋ on chiD and the index i + 1 on muTil, and rhoDetPrime_eq_muTilde_mul_chi_pow uses the exponent ⌊N(i)/2⌋.
In D7, etaJ_tie applies for 1 ≤ j ≤ m, and Y_sigval applies for j ≤ m.
In D7, jetL uses the level jOf i − 1 and jetL1 uses the level j1Of i − 1.
In Ranks, k and m are even, t is odd, 2 ≤ m, m + 3 ≤ k, k + m − 1 + 5 ≤ t, 3m < t, m ≤ 2·ord, 2·ord ≤ k and m² ≤ k + m(t + 1).
In HCParam, e j − b j ≥ (t + 3)/2 and b(j+1) − e j ≥ (t + 3)/2, each u i is an integer plus 1/2, and v, b and e are integers.
In Host, QS ≤ n², o^64 ≤ 2^e, q ≠ 3, and 4·t·r + 1 is less than both q and d.
In Host, every odd prime p ≤ splitBound has Jacobi symbol (−d/p) = 1, and every odd prime l dividing QS satisfies 4·l ≤ splitBound.

In Host, pde and pde' leave remainder 1 on division by 15, the norm of ccK is coprime to 2, 3, 5, q, d, QS and all level primes, and ccK is not contained in the ideal generated by any integer greater than 1.
In Host, 2 ≤ Lw and every s in T2 satisfies 4·Lw·s < n0, and NoRel forbids relations with integer coefficients i, j satisfying 0 < |i| ≤ Lw and 0 < |j| ≤ Lw.
In HostRaw, 2 ≤ e, 0 < QS, 2^(e+2) divides QS, QS is coprime to q·d, and the cyclotomic field used has conductor QS·q·d.
In HostHyp, q and d are primes with q ≡ 3 mod 8, d ≡ 7 mod 16 and Jacobi symbol (−d/q) = 1.

In HostDer, E has degree 4·ord over the rationals, F has degree 2·ord, the CM type has 2·ord elements, the discriminant of E is the square of that of F, 2^(e + 1 − 2^(−e))·√d ≤ rd ≤ (QS/2)·√(q·d) and 4·ord ≤ rd².
In GIdx, the prime p must satisfy 5 ≤ p.
In ColumnChain, DGam > 0 and the values rhoDet and rhoDet' have absolute value 1 for i < m.
In ColumnsAtT, vT has f elements, each field Fv has T elements, duStar > 0, Dstar > 0 and GamP > 1.
In DivData, delP ≤ 1.
In Rows.Data, Tau has f elements, delp ≤ 1, Drows = (1 − delp)·Dall, restRowsFiniteGroupCard > 0, and etaJ and shaLen are nonnegative.
In Rows.Places, every ramification index is positive.

In MemberForms, the spaces lv and lk have dimension N i, the weight sg has length N m − 1, the formula for lam uses blocks of size t + 1 after the first k entries, and beOn and thFree are nonnegative.
In wG, the weight is e j − k/2 − (2j − 1)(t + 1)/2, and in rhoVec the shift is (N − 1)/2 − i.
In Spaces, X j has rank N j for j ≤ m, W j has rank r and V j has rank nV for 1 ≤ j ≤ m, zm has Hermitian norm −T, and the hyperbolic pairs pair to 1.
In CMData and in LocAt, the extension has degree 2.

In NData, sha_eq applies for 0 < e < t, 1 ≤ j i ≤ m, chi_def applies for 1 ≤ c ≤ t with exponent −(c − 1), s0 i = max(1, exponent of l i in QS) for odd l i, T_gen uses 1 ≤ k ≤ nV, PlG k has f elements, and the labels have degree r.

In NTw, the inertia image of delta has exactly 15 elements, places in pD have norm ≡ 1 mod 15, chi1 raised to the power g k − 1 is trivial at tame places, zk is a primitive l^k-th root of unity, and 1 ≤ jS ≤ m and 1 ≤ jL ≤ m.
In NTh, aL equals 1 when l i is some g k and 0 otherwise, and hk_ev applies for 1 ≤ k ≤ r.
In NBC, satAU has nV/2 elements and infW has nV elements, each an integer plus (nV − 1)/2.
In NAut, etaT has Frobenius eigenvalue −1 at non-split places, regular algebraic parameters are integers plus (a − 1)/2, and chi_mu uses the twist (t − 1)/2 + (1 − nV)/2.

In NTypes, every g k ≡ 1 mod QS·q·d, Mray is unramified outside primes dividing QS·q·d, the pairs in bc σ have positive entries with sum of products equal to r, and the polynomials in labPar and eSer have degree r.
In heckePol, the polynomial has degree nV and uses the power k(k − 1)/2 of the norm.
In JetLoc and JetLoc1, the prime l satisfies 5 ≤ l, and in JetLoc d is even with 2 ≤ d.
In ThetaJet, 1 ≤ jOf i ≤ m and 1 ≤ j1Of i ≤ m.

In SData, Del > 0, consecutive v entries differ by 4·Del, the letter sequences have length k − 2, u(l+1) = v l − 1/2 − Del or v l − 1/2, all scales and volumes are positive, and points live in dimension rS + 1.
In sigYD, the signature is (rankY j − ⌊(m − j)/2⌋, ⌊(m − j)/2⌋).
In CDHaar, the density constant c is neither 0 nor infinite.
In HidaSetting, 5 ≤ p, n' is even with 2 ≤ n', the residue ring has p^n' elements and w² = p.
In LocPrime and LocAinf, v(l) = 1, ζ 0 = 1, ζ 1 ≠ 1, and χQ agrees with an integer up to l^(−m).
In PeriodData, t lies in Fil 1 and not in Fil 2, and φ t = p·t.
In GoodCoef, the roots of unity considered have order dividing lcm(l, N).
In IsGood, the polynomials have degree N, for every a with 1 ≤ a and 2a ≤ N some polynomial has no factor of degree a, and some irreducible factor has prime degree q with N < 2q and q + 3 ≤ N.
In Exc, a prime ℓ counts as exceptional when g^d < ℓ^(4·v), where v is the exponent of ℓ in g^d − 1, and BB uses 1 ≤ d ≤ N.
